##

In an era where technological advancements, particularly artificial intelligence (AI), are reshaping industries at a fast pace, the job market is undergoing significant transformation. The potential obsolescence of traditional skills due to AI-driven productivity is a common concern. Therefore, it is crucial to comprehensively assess the employability of Indian graduates for the right skills to build the future workforce.

The second edition of the report on the employability of Indian graduates, India’s Graduate Skill Index 2025, published by Mercer | Mettl, arrives at a pivotal moment as AI continues to transform industries and redefine job roles. This edition refines its methodology to better fit the needs of the Indian graduates in the job market, ensuring that the insights provided are both relevant and actionable.

28% of employers anticipate that a substantial transformation of technical skills will be necessary for about one-third of their talent base in 2025 to remain competitive in the corporate world.

## Graduate employability landscape in India

As businesses continue to leverage AI to enhance efficiency, improve customer experiences, and drive innovation, Indian industries are positioning themselves as a key player in the global AI landscape. This boom presents opportunities for economic growth and underscores the need for a skilled workforce capable of harnessing the potential of AI technologies.

The AI market in India is projected to reach US$17 billion – US$22 billion by 2027, growing at a CAGR of 25%-35%.

The IndiaAI mission, launched by the Indian government with a budget of Rs.10,371.92 crore, aims to foster AI innovation across the country. The mission encompasses several key components aimed at creating a robust AI ecosystem in the country. IndiaAI compute capacity, innovation center, application development initiative and datasets platform are the key components of the mission aimed at fostering the vision of Making AI in India. Moreover, the IndiaAI future skills program aims to expand AI education and establish data and AI labs in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, nurturing the aspirations of Gen Z students.

Consequentially, identifying and assessing graduates with the right skills becomes crucial for industries to build a competent and adaptable workforce. By focusing on the relevant skills, such as data analytics and AI proficiency, graduates can contribute effectively from day one. Meanwhile, strong soft skills—such as communication, teamwork, learning agility, etc.— enable graduates to interact better with AI and navigate complex workplace dynamics.

## Key findings from the Mercer | Mettl India's Graduate Skill Index 2025

According to Mercer | Mettl’s findings, the overall employability of Indian graduates has slightly decreased to 42.6% in 2024 from 44.3% in 2023. The decline is primarily driven by a drop in employability for non-technical roles, while employability in technical roles has seen an increase. 46% of graduates are now employable in AI and machine learning roles, reflecting a significant increase in proficiency in these technical skills.

- Male graduates exhibit a marginally higher employability rate of 43.4% compared to 41.7% for female graduates, indicating a balance of competence across the two genders.

- Graduates from Tier 1 colleges demonstrate the highest employability rates at 48.4%, followed by Tier 2 colleges at 46.1% and Tier 3 colleges at 43.4%. This variation highlights the need for institutions to improve educational quality and align curricula with industry demands in both technical and non-technical roles.

- Delhi, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, and Uttarakhand demonstrate higher employability rates, while Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Assam, and Telangana also rank among the top 10 states.

- With an overall 50% employability, there has been a great emphasis on the increasing demand for soft skills, with communication, critical thinking, and leadership being the most sought-after attributes. However, there remains room for improvement in creativity. As AI continues to reshape the job market, employers prioritize candidates who can collaborate effectively, think critically, and demonstrate high learning agility.

Download the report

## How to leverage graduate employability data for workforce planning

The report methodology assessed data collected from over 2,700 campuses and 1 million learners from 30+ states and union territories. This extensive analysis ensures a robust and reliable foundation for the report’s findings.

India’s Graduate Skill Index 2025 report serves as a critical resource as it can help organizations and academia enhance their workforce development strategies significantly.

- By utilizing the insights, employers can refine their hiring processes to focus on the specific skills and competencies that are in high demand, ensuring they attract candidates who are not only technically proficient but also possess essential soft skills.

- Educational institutions can align their curricula with industry demands, ensuring that students acquire the job-specific skills as well as soft skills that employers are seeking.

- Institutes can leverage the report to design targeted training and development programs, workshops, and extracurricular activities that focus on enhancing critical thinking, communication, and leadership abilities among students.

By actively engaging with the findings of the report, organizations and academic institutions can improve their training programs and offerings, respectively, and contribute to producing a workforce that is well-equipped to meet the challenges of an AI-driven economy.

## Conclusion

As organizations adapt their strategies and embrace digital transformation, the demand for skilled graduates is expected to rise. While the prospects for graduates appear promising, the path to success in an AI-driven and hyper-connected workplace is fraught with challenges. In 2023, India experienced a notable slump in volume hiring for graduates, primarily due to a slowdown in the IT industry, which traditionally recruits thousands of graduates annually. Following a hiring boom in previous years, major IT companies have had to reduce their headcount in response to a conservative client market in the West, inflation, high interest rates, and various other geopolitical factors.

However, industry experts anticipate a promising turnaround in the future as companies prepare for a hiring spree, signaling a revival in demand for entry-level talent. This shift presents a valuable opportunity for graduates to capitalize on the evolving landscape and secure their place in the burgeoning AI market. Encouraging signs of growth are already emerging, highlighting a bright outlook for new entrants in the industry.

Undoubtedly, a systematic approach to skill assessment can help organizations identify potential gaps in their workforce and hire the right talent. This proactive strategy not only improves employee performance but also fosters a culture of continuous learning, ensuring that the workforce remains competitive in a rapidly changing environment. Ultimately, aligning graduate skills with industry requirements is essential for driving organizational success and maintaining a robust talent pipeline.

## About the Mercer | Mettl Business Aptitude Test

### What is the importance of business analysts in an organization?

Business analysts perform market research to identify business needs and procure data to perform related analyses and recommend solutions to help organizations achieve their goals. Analysts require a strong grasp of analytical reasoning, data analysis, and critical thinking in order to measure and monitor business growth and risks. In addition, they should also have strong communication skills so that business messages are conveyed precisely and clearly.

### What roles can you assess using this test?

- Business analysts – Analytics: They leverage data analytics to assess processes, determine requirements, deliver data-informed reports and recommendations to executives and stakeholders and propose methods for organizations to enhance efficiency. They collect and analyze data to explore and develop potential solutions, including enhancements to systems and processes. This test evaluates candidates' analytical skills and ability to interpret data effectively, ensuring they provide valuable insights that drive organizational improvements.

- Business analysts - Data and technology: They assess the organization's current data and technology and engage with stakeholders to understand the system's effectiveness and identify areas for improvement. They also suggest solutions, including upgrades and installations, to enhance productivity, align with the organization's goals and strategies, and resolve issues. This position necessitates staying updated on the latest trends in data and technology. This test helps identify candidates with strong technical knowledge and problem-solving abilities, helping address the organization's data and technology needs.

- Business intelligence analysts: They help organizations interpret the large amounts of data they have, supporting businesses in optimizing processes, enhancing profitability, and keeping up with industry trends. They are skilled professionals with technical and analytical expertise who evaluate data, communicate relevant findings to the business, and present them in a way that can drive effective change. ## Pertanyaan Umum

###
### Ada berapa jenis tes kemampuan profesional yang tersedia?

Ada beberapa jenis tes kemampuan profesional yang dirancang untuk menilai berbagai keterampilan dan kemampuan. Tes kemampuan secara umum dapat dikategorikan menjadi dua kelompok utama: tes kemampuan khusus dan tes kemampuan umum.Tes kemampuan khusus menilai keterampilan atau kemampuan yang berkaitan dengan pekerjaan atau bidang studi tertentu. Sebagai contoh, tes kemampuan verbal digunakan untuk menilai keterampilan bahasa dan kemampuan penalaran kandidat.Di sisi lain, tes kemampuan umum mengukur berbagai kemampuan kognitif dengan menggunakan tes seperti tes penalaran numerik, tes penalaran verbal, tes penalaran abstrak, dan tes kemampuan berpikir kritis.Beberapa jenis tes kemampuan profesional yang populer dalam kedua kategori tersebut adalah sebagai berikut.

-
Tes kemampuan Umum: Tes kemampuan prakerja ini digunakan oleh tim SDM untuk menilai kemampuan kognitif pelamar, termasuk penalaran, keterampilan numerik, keterampilan analisis data, dan keterampilan verbal.

-
Tes Penalaran Logis: asesmen ini mengevaluasi kemampuan penalaran kandidat dan kemampuan mereka untuk menganalisis informasi dari berbagai perspektif dan menarik kesimpulan.

-
Tes Penalaran Spasial: Tes ini mengukur kemampuan kandidat untuk memahami dan memvisualisasikan pola dan bentuk dua dimensi dan tiga dimensi.

-
Tes Pengambilan Keputusan: Tes ini menilai kemampuan kandidat untuk melihat berbagai aspek dari sebuah masalah dan menemukan solusi dengan menggunakan keterampilan dan pengetahuan yang dimiliki.

###
### Bagaimana tes kemampuan pekerjaan dapat membantu pemberi kerja?

Tes kemampuan pekerjaan memberikan wawasan berharga tentang kemampuan pemecahan masalah, keterampilan berpikir kritis, dan kemampuan kognitif secara keseluruhan dari seorang kandidat. Pemberi kerja dapat menggunakan asesmen ini untuk mengidentifikasi kandidat yang berpotensi unggul dalam peran mereka.

###
### Apakah tes kemampuan hanya untuk posisi tingkat pemula?

Tidak. asesmen kemampuan dapat digunakan untuk mengevaluasi kandidat di semua tingkat, dari tingkat pemula hingga posisi eksekutif. asesmen ini dapat membantu mengidentifikasi kandidat yang sesuai dengan kemampuan kognitif yang tepat dan potensi pertumbuhan yang baik dalam organisasi.

###
### Apa perbedaan antara asesmen kognitif dan asesmen kemampuan?

asesmen kognitif mengukur kemampuan intelektual secara keseluruhan, termasuk daya ingat, perhatian, pemecahan masalah, dan kecepatan pemrosesan informasi. Sementara itu, tes kemampuan berfokus pada kemampuan atau kemampuan spesifik yang relevan dengan pekerjaan atau bidang tertentu yang membantu pemberi kerja menilai kecocokan individu untuk suatu peran.

###
### 6. Bagaimana tes kognitif karyawan dapat digunakan untuk mengidentifikasi aspek-aspek yang perlu ditingkatkan dan memberikan kesempatan pelatihan dan pengembangan yang terarah?

Tes kognitif online dapat digunakan untuk mengidentifikasi aspek-aspek yang perlu ditingkatkan bagi karyawan dengan menilai keterampilan dan kemampuan mereka. Tes ini juga dapat mengidentifikasi aspek-aspek yang mungkin memerlukan pelatihan atau pengembangan tambahan. Hal ini dapat membantu menyediakan kesempatan pelatihan dan pengembangan yang terarah untuk meningkatkan keterampilan karyawan.

###
### Bagaimana sistem asesmen tes kemampuan?

Tes kemampuan dinilai berdasarkan berbagai metode tergantung jenis tes dan metode yang diadopsi oleh organisasi. Beberapa metode standar untuk menilai tes kemampuan adalah sebagai berikut.

-
Skor mentah: Kandidat mendapat skor atas setiap jawaban yang benar. Misalnya, jika tes berisi 50 pertanyaan dan kandidat menjawab 40 pertanyaan dengan benar, maka skor mentahnya adalah 40.

-
Skor berskala: Metode penilaian ini memperhitungkan variasi kesulitan dalam berbagai versi dari tes yang sama. Metode ini membantu membandingkan skor di berbagai penyelenggaraan tes. Skor berskala biasanya dilaporkan dalam skala, seperti 0 hingga 100 atau 200 hingga 800.

-
Peringkat Persentil: Metode ini menunjukkan persentase orang yang mendapat skor lebih rendah dari Anda. Misalnya, jika seorang kandidat berada di persentil ke-70, itu berarti kandidat tersebut mendapat skor lebih tinggi daripada 70% dari orang-orang yang mengikuti tes tersebut.

-
Skor standar: Skor ini telah diubah menjadi nilai rata-rata 100 dan standar deviasi 15. Jenis skor ini umum digunakan dalam tes seperti Tes Bakat Skolastik (SAT).

-
Skor gabungan: Skor ini menggabungkan skor dari beberapa bagian atau subtes dari suatu tes.

-
Lulus/Gagal: Dalam banyak kasus, tes kemampuan digunakan untuk menentukan keputusan lulus/gagal. Jika seseorang mencapai skor tertentu, maka mereka 'lulus' tes tersebut.

-
Teori Respons Butir: Metode ini lebih kompleks karena tidak hanya mempertimbangkan pertanyaan mana yang dijawab dengan benar oleh kandidat tetapi juga kesulitan setiap pertanyaan dan kemungkinan menjawab benar berdasarkan kinerja keseluruhan kandidat.

###
### Apa keuntungan dari tes kemampuan kognitif online?

Terdapat beberapa alasan mengapa organisasi harus mempertimbangkan menggunakan tes kognitif online untuk perekrutan. Di antara alasan tersebut adalah sebagai berikut.

-
Efisiensi dan kenyamanan: Tes kognitif yang dilakukan secara online memungkinkan kandidat mengikuti asesmen dari mana saja dengan koneksi internet yang stabil. Oleh karena itu, asesmen tatap muka tidak diperlukan sehingga menghemat waktu dan sumber daya.

-
Skalabilitas: Platform tes kognitif online dapat dengan mudah mengakomodasi banyak kandidat secara bersamaan. Hal ini sangat berguna bagi perusahaan yang melakukan perekrutan massal atau memiliki kebutuhan perekrutan dalam jumlah besar.

-
Standardisasi: Tes kognitif online menyediakan proses evaluasi yang konsisten. Pertanyaan dan kriteria asesmen telah ditentukan sebelumnya sehingga mengurangi bias dalam asesmen. Standardisasi ini membantu dalam membuat keputusan perekrutan yang adil dan objektif.

-
Efektivitas biaya: Tes kognitif online lebih hemat biaya jika dibandingkan dengan asesmen tradisional. Tes ini tidak memerlukan biaya yang berkaitan dengan pusat asesmen fisik, pencetakan, pengiriman, dan penyimpanan materi tes fisik.

## Introduction

Performance and potential reviews are often used interchangeably, but these are two completely different concepts. While performance evaluation focuses on employees’ performance over a period, the potential review aims to evaluate candidates’ latent skills and talents.

Both performance and potential review play an important role in career development and growth. They are used to hire skilled candidates, determine appropriate compensation, identify high-potential employees, develop L&D programs, and plan succession.

This blog looks at vital differences between performance and potential review and their uses.

## What is a performance review?

A performance review is a tool used to evaluate employees’ accomplishments over a period, which is usually a year. Performance evaluation includes both qualitative and quantitative aspects of the role. The review generally measures how successful the employee was in completing their tasks, which is evaluated against a set standard for the job role.

## Objectives of a performance review

Common objectives of a performance review are:

Setting goals

Assigning employee goals and targets is a primary objective of performance evaluation. Setting up goals helps employees know and understand what is expected from them. It also allows managers to measure workers’ performance levels easily.

For assigning targets, last year’s performance review should be taken as a basis. Also, clearly describe the areas of improvement and the aspects to be evaluated in the following evaluation cycle. Finally, consider your employees’ opinions to avoid burdening them with unachievable expectations. It is imperative to discuss the time, resources, and other help they need to accomplish set goals.

Counsel and motivate employees

According to research by Great Place to Work, 37% of employees said personal recognition would encourage them to work better.

Performance reviews are a perfect time to let employees know what they are doing right and the areas they need to work on. On the one hand, the discussion helps you motivate hardworking employees to aim higher and, on the other, understand why some were lacking in certain areas or underperforming.

The insights thus gained help you plan targets better and allot your resources where needed. For example, an employee might need additional aid to complete a task, which might be allotted to them for the coming performance cycle.

Plan for raises and promotions

Raises and promotions are often tied with the performance review. As you measure an employee’s performance by reviewing their goals for the previous period, it is easier to identify team members who are high performing. It makes raises and promotions forthright.

Staff planning

Performance evaluation helps you recognize the well-staffed departments and the ones that require additional talent to get the job done. In addition, regular performance reviews help you pinpoint roles where employees are being stretched thin or working beyond their bandwidth, helping build a case for hiring more employees.

Plan learning and development programs

Another area where performance evaluation helps is ascertaining the employees that need additional training to upgrade their skills. After recognizing several workers’ training needs, you can easily plan your learning and development (L&D) programs depending on the group size and budget.

## What is a potential review?

Potential review can be defined as identifying qualities and abilities in a candidate or employee that they may possess but still need to develop fully. Potential evaluation helps organizations decide if a candidate is worth hiring or not. Apart from helping in hiring, potential evaluation is often a part of a performance review. A worker’s talent and skills are identified to chart a career path for them or prepare them for new responsibilities.

Indicators of potential

- Ability to act objectively without getting influenced by emotional/personal bias.

- The capability to think beyond the conventional solutions to a problem.

- The skill to manage complicated situations and challenges.

- The ability to examine a situation from multiple viewpoints.

## Objectives of a potential review

Potential review is mainly done to fulfill the following objectives:

### Identify the candidate with the most potential

Recruiters must not judge a candidate just based on their technical skills. They also need to assess a candidate’s other traits, which is where potential review comes in. It helps HRs shortlist candidates who show the most potential and would be an excellent fit for the organization.

### Identify high-potential employees

The potential review helps you identify employees with the inherent talent to take up senior roles. Such employees can be easily trained for suitable promotions.

### Identify training needs

Performance review and potential evaluation help you plan a training program for your employees. The potential review enables you to identify areas that require training. This helps grow and develop employees’ skills and makes them loyal to the organization invested in their development.

### Plan succession

Potential evaluation helps you identify high-potential (HIPO) employees. In addition, by recognizing such employees who can fill vacant positions, the potential review makes it easier for an organization to arrange and carry out succession planning activities.

### Assist employees in the personal development process

A potential review also helps employees become aware of their areas of strength. This allows them to plan their personal development effectively by discussing training and upskilling plans with their employers.

## Difference between potential and performance review

Organizations use performance reviews to evaluate and rate employees’ performance and contribution toward the company’s goal. An employee who meets the set goals or targets is recognized through rewards and appreciation. The rewards can be in the form of salary hikes or promotions. Thus, performance appraisal acts as a link between employees’ careers and the organization’s goals.

Potential review, on the other hand, is used to identify an individual’s latent skills and talents. Identifying these skills helps an organization prepare the individual for higher responsibilities or decide if the candidate is a good fit. Thus, the potential review is a tool for hiring and succession planning.

Here is a look at other critical differences between performance and potential review:

Past vs. future-oriented

Performance review considers employees’ achievements for the past year. It measures them against goals set at the end of the previous performance appraisal. Furthermore, managers set targets for the next cycle depending on the past year’s accomplishments. This makes performance evaluation both a past and future-oriented activity.

On the other hand, a potential review is a future-oriented activity and sometimes a part of a performance review. The potential review helps managers ascertain the hidden talent and skills of employees. Which is then used to chart employee career progression, prepare training programs, and plan promotions and successions.

Timing

Performance review is usually an annual cycle. Employees’ accomplishments over time are measured against a standard or the previous year’s performance.

The potential review usually takes place during the hiring process to gauge a candidate’s organizational fit or later either as a part of performance evaluation or as a stand-alone process for succession planning or L&D programs.

Users

Performance evaluation is a tool used by managers to know who in their team is meeting targets, who are falling short, and the reasons behind it. On the other hand, a potential review is mainly used by recruiters to make better hiring decisions and plan training and development programs.

Data required

To conduct a performance review, managers need data from previous reviews as employees are measured against it. In this way, managers check the growth shown by a particular employee.

As for a potential review, no data is needed from the previous review. Instead, HRs can rely on assessment tests to appraise a candidate’s potential and make appropriate hiring decisions.

## How Mercer | Mettl can help

Whether you are looking to conduct an annual employee performance review or need help with a potential candidate appraisal, Mercer | Mettl has a host of solutions for you. With Mercer | Mettl, you can quickly and accurately assess candidates, run performance reviews, and evaluate strategic employee development and training needs accordingly.

If you are looking for a solution for potential review, Mercer | Mettl’s pre-employment assessments are the answers. These assessments enable you to ascertain and measure candidates’ core traits and acquired skills. The assessments include personality, behavioral, cognitive, and communication skills assessments, among others. They ensure you get well-rounded insights into candidates’ potential, skills, and talents. With Mercer | Mettl, you can:

- Curate customized assessments

- Schedule and invite multiple candidates

- Get real-time results and customized reports

As for performance reviews, Mercer | Mettl’s 360 Degree Feedback Tool takes care of it. The review mechanism differs from conventional assessment software as it uses a multi-rater approach. The tool collects ratings from multiple sources, like peers, managers, and clients. Apart from making the performance evaluation seamless, the 360 Degree Feedback Tool also helps you:

- Identify gaps in skills as perceived by other stakeholders

- Identify high-potential (HIPO) employees

- Get a holistic overview of an employee’s performance

## Conclusion

Both potential and performance appraisal are essential for an organization that wants to get the best out of its employees. Using them to hire, develop a training plan, and plan succession can help you achieve your organizational goals.

## Frequently asked questions (FAQs)

###
### What are the main types of behavioral assessments?

Behavioral assessments come in various forms, each designed to evaluate different aspects of a person's workplace behavior. The main types of behavioral assessments include personality tests, situational judgement tests, work simulations, direct and indirect assessments, and culture fit evaluations.

###
### What are behavioral assessments used for?

Behavioral assessments are commonly used for recruitment and development initiatives to measure critical competencies required to perform on the job in an organization. Behavioral assessments require individuals to demonstrate behavioral competencies in one or more activities relevant to their job role and resemble an actual organizational situation. Candidates are presented with a series of realistic work-related scenarios with possible actions to be taken. They have to select either the best option or rank the possible actions based on their effectiveness.

###
### What do behavioral tests measure?

Behavioral tests measure behavioral competencies. Behavioral competencies are a combination of skills, knowledge, and traits in an individual. Behavioral competencies are a job’s components that reflect in behavior and are observable in the workplace. Behavioral competencies often vary across job levels and job roles. Each behavioral competency can be measured through varied combinations of behavior test, the results of which can help in better workforce planning.

###
### What are the features of behavioral assessment?

One of the features of behavioral assessments is that they can measure a plethora of behavioral competencies and tendencies. They are created based on specific job functions i.e. they are customized to emulate a specific job’s realities, posing questions that reflect actual workplace situations. Behavioral assessments can be administered via virtual assessment centers, making them highly time and cost-effective, and easily scalable. Behavioral assessments can be easily combined with other tools for a holistic evaluation.

###
### What is an example of a behavioral assessment?

An example of a behavioral assessment is the Mercer | Mettl Personality Map – Forced Choice (MPM-FC). The assessment helps understand how people are likely to behave at work by asking them to choose between statements that all seem equally positive. This makes it harder for the candidate to guess the ‘right’ answer and gives a more honest view of their behavior. The assessment looks at important workplace traits like teamwork, adaptability, and initiative. MPM-FC is useful in hiring, promotions, and employee development, giving a clear and well-rounded picture of each person.

## About the Mercer SQL Developer (Basic) Assessment

The Mercer SQL Developer (Basic) Assessment is a structured pre-employment test designed to evaluate candidates’ fundamental understanding of SQL and their ability to apply database concepts in practical work environments. It measures knowledge of database queries, data manipulation techniques, and core SQL operations that are commonly required in entry-level database and software development roles.

Rather than focusing only on theoretical familiarity, the assessment evaluates how effectively individuals apply SQL knowledge to routine database tasks. It assesses the ability to retrieve and manipulate data, work with database objects, and use SQL commands within scenarios that reflect day-to-day development and data management activities. This provides organizations with objective insight into candidates’ applied SQL capability and technical readiness.

Developed to support consistent technical screening, the assessment enables hiring teams to evaluate candidates using uniform criteria before progressing them to interviews or role-specific evaluations. The result is a more objective view of foundational database capability, helping organizations identify individuals who can effectively contribute to junior database, analytics, and software development environments.

### Benefits of using the SQL Developer (Basic) Assessment

The SQL Developer (Basic) Assessment helps organizations bring greater consistency and objectivity into early-stage technical hiring. Using a systematic framework to evaluate SQL knowledge, the test provides clear insight into candidates’ database development capabilities before they progress to interviews or role-specific evaluations.

-

Standardized technical screening: Provides a consistent approach to evaluating foundational SQL skills across candidates, enabling fair and comparable assessment.

-

Objective validation of database skills: Assesses candidates’ ability to write queries, manipulate data, and apply SQL concepts in practical workplace scenarios rather than relying on self-reported experience.

-

Improved early-stage shortlisting: Helps identify candidates who meet baseline technical requirements, allowing recruiters to focus on the most suitable applicants.

-

Less reliance on resumes alone: Provides measurable evidence of SQL capability, helping organizations evaluate candidates beyond qualifications and project descriptions.

-

More focused technical interviews: Enables interviewers to concentrate on deeper technical discussions and role-specific requirements rather than validating foundational SQL knowledge.

-

Reduced hiring risk: Evaluates job-relevant database skills early in the recruitment process, helping organizations identify candidates who are prepared for SQL-related responsibilities.

-

Scalable hiring support: Supports both individual hiring needs and large-scale recruitment initiatives with consistent evaluation standards across candidate pools.

### Why should organizations use the SQL Developer (Basic) Assessment in recruitment?

Organizations hiring for SQL-focused roles need to determine whether candidates can work effectively with databases, retrieve information accurately, and apply SQL concepts in practical environments. However, exposure to SQL varies considerably across applicants, making it difficult to assess technical readiness solely from resumes and interviews. A structured assessment establishes a consistent benchmark for measuring foundational SQL capability and supports more objective hiring decisions.

-

SQL proficiency varies across candidate backgrounds: Individuals may acquire SQL knowledge through academic programs, certifications, self-learning, or workplace experience, making direct comparisons difficult without a regularized evaluation framework.

-

Practical application matters as much as conceptual knowledge: Understanding SQL principles does not necessarily indicate the ability to retrieve, manipulate, and manage data in real database environments.

-

Resumes provide limited visibility into technical depth: Technology lists and project descriptions may indicate exposure to SQL, but they may not accurately reflect practical capability or problem-solving ability.

-

Consistent evaluation standards are essential: SQL-related roles frequently attract candidates from varied educational and professional backgrounds, and require objective, comparable assessment criteria.

-

Foundational SQL skills support day-to-day responsibilities: Activities such as reporting, application development, and database maintenance rely on accurate query writing and effective data handling.

-

Early validation strengthens technical screening: Assessing SQL capability before interviews and advanced evaluations helps create a more structured, efficient recruitment process.

### How does our SQL Developer (Basic) Assessment work?

The SQL Developer (Basic) Assessment follows a systematic evaluation approach to measure candidates’ understanding of SQL concepts and their ability to apply them in practical data and database scenarios. The assessment combines domain-focused questions with tasks that reflect how SQL is used in routine development and data management activities. This helps organizations evaluate both conceptual understanding and applied technical capability.

Junior software developer

Junior software developers support software development activities by writing code, resolving defects, and helping maintain application functionality under established development processes. Many entry-level development roles require working with databases to retrieve, update, and manage application data. The SQL Developer (Basic) Assessment helps evaluate whether candidates possess the SQL knowledge required to work with relational databases and can support database-driven applications.

-

Database analyst

Database analysts are responsible for organizing, analyzing, and managing data within structured database environments. Their work involves query creation, validating information, supporting reporting requirements, and ensuring that databases continue to meet business needs. The assessment helps determine whether candidates can work with database objects, write accurate SQL queries, and apply database concepts required for routine analytical and database management responsibilities.

-

Oracle SQL developer

Oracle SQL developers specialize in developing and maintaining database solutions using SQL and related database technologies. Their responsibilities include writing queries, developing database objects, supporting data operations, and optimizing database performance. The SQL Developer (Basic) Assessment helps evaluate whether candidates demonstrate the core SQL proficiency that is required to work with database structures, create queries, and support day-to-day database development activities.

-

Database developer

Database developers design, build, and maintain database components that support business applications and reporting systems. They work with tables, views, queries, and other database objects to ensure data is stored, accessed, and managed efficiently. The assessment helps identify candidates who understand core SQL concepts and can apply them within structured database development environments.

-

Data analyst

Data analysts use data to support reporting, operational monitoring, and business decision-making. A significant portion of their work involves retrieving, filtering, and organizing information from relational databases. The assessment evaluates candidates’ ability to write queries, work with structured datasets, and apply SQL techniques supporting data analysis and reporting activities.

-

Application support analyst

Application support analysts often investigate system issues, validate application data, and support operational processes that rely on database systems. Their responsibilities may require querying databases to troubleshoot problems and verify information. The assessment helps determine whether candidates possess the SQL fundamentals needed to work effectively with application data and database-driven systems.

## Introduction

Hackathons accelerate innovation by driving teams to create breakthrough solutions, test new ideas, and identify standout talent. Yet many organizations struggle to translate this energy into clear business outcomes due to a lack of transparent, consistent evaluation criteria. Without such a framework, valuable concepts may be missed, and participants often remain unclear about how their work was assessed or how to improve.

Organizations must establish an evaluation system that aligns innovation with strategic priorities, ensures impartial and credible assessment, and provides meaningful feedback, turning each hackathon from a momentary event into a lasting driver of business value.

## Hackathon: Understanding its meaning and purpose

A hackathon is an immersive innovation challenge where people from diverse fields join individually or in teams to tackle a specific problem or experiment with a bold new idea, all within a short, fixed timeframe. In these sessions, participants move from initial concepts to working prototypes at remarkable speed, often producing in days what might otherwise take months.

Organizations host hackathons to inject fresh ideas into their innovation pipeline, stress-test concepts in real-world conditions, and spot individuals who excel when creativity and urgency meet. The format blends design thinking, rapid development, and live problem-solving into a single, high-impact experience.

Teams participating in hackathons usually bring together coders, designers, strategists, and domain experts, pooling their strengths to create a functional solution. Throughout the event, they research, experiment, adjust, and refine until they are ready to present to peers, decision‑makers, or a judging panel. Many hackathons also welcome individual participants who often work independently, exploring ideas with more freedom while engaging through shared feedback, mentorship, and other opportunities.

When well-executed, hackathons do more than generate promising ideas. They foster cross‑disciplinary collaboration, unearth unconventional approaches, and deliver solutions that can go directly into production.

Many breakthroughs from internal process improvements to market-ready apps have begun at hackathons, proving their value as a powerful driver of business impact and a springboard for discovering exceptional talent.

## Guiding innovation: Understanding the role of hackathon mentors

Hackathon mentors are experienced professionals who guide and support participants throughout the event, helping them refine ideas, solve problems, and build effective solutions. They bring specialized knowledge from their fields and use it to accelerate the progress of teams working under tight deadlines.

A mentor’s role can take many forms. Some focus on improving the creative and design aspects of a project, offering advice on originality, visual appeal, and user experience. Others contribute deep expertise in specific industries or business processes, helping teams align their solutions with practical realities. Many mentors possess strong technical skills, enabling them to troubleshoot complex issues, suggest better architectures, or recommend more efficient tools.

During in-person hackathons, mentors often work on a rotation, moving from team to team, answering questions, and offering on-the-spot guidance. In virtual settings, they connect with participants through dedicated channels, video calls, or collaborative platforms, making their expertise accessible regardless of location. In both formats, effective mentors remain aligned with the hackathon’s core objectives and themes so that their input guides the event toward its intended outcomes.

Mentors can come from a variety of professional backgrounds, including senior technologists such as software architects, project managers, analysts, and developers. They may be chief technology or information officers, startup founders, marketing strategists, business development specialists, or project directors. Strong mentorship can mean the difference between an idea that fades and one that emerges as a winning, high-impact solution.

## Benefits of having mentors at a hackathon

Mentors turn hackathons from a creative exercise into a strategic advantage. They guide teams through tough challenges, offer expert insights, and help transform bold ideas into solutions that drive measurable business results. Some of the major advantages of having mentors at hackathons include:

- Maintaining momentum when pressure peaks: Hackathon schedules can be intense, and teams may lose focus when deadlines close in. By encouraging participants, clarifying priorities, and reinforcing belief in their abilities, mentors help them push through demanding phases without losing direction or energy.

- Turning creative concepts into practical solutions: Mentors apply sector expertise to shape ambitious ideas into workable plans. Their guidance balances innovation with commercial and technical realities, steering teams away from unworkable paths and toward solutions that can be built and scaled effectively.

- Creating pathways to influential networks: With extensive professional contacts, mentors connect participants to key stakeholders, investors, and potential partners. These introductions can extend the life of a project beyond the event and open doors to strategic collaborations.

- Providing rapid and targeted input: Mentors give constructive feedback while projects are still evolving. This on‑the‑spot advice allows teams to adjust designs, improve functionality, and fine‑tune presentations in real time, maximizing the value of the limited hackathon window.

## Hackathon judges: Who they are and what they do

In every hackathon, judges serve as the vital link between creativity and recognized achievement. Their role is dynamic; not only do they evaluate projects on innovation, impact, and feasibility, but they also provide meaningful feedback, encouraging participants to grow and refine their skills.

Choosing the most suitable judges is a critical step toward a credible and inspiring competition. Organizers should seek out a panel that blends deep domain knowledge with varied perspectives, ensuring that technical prowess, user experience, business strategy, and scalability all receive adequate attention. Including respected industry figures, influential academics, and specialists known for evaluating fresh ideas can raise the event’s profile and motivate participants to strive for excellence.

Effective judge selection begins with identifying professionals whose expertise aligns closely with the hackathon’s focus. The panel should be diverse, drawing voices from technology, business, design, and sector-specific backgrounds to foster balanced and comprehensive evaluation.

Recruiting judges early allows time to confirm availability and create a diverse bench of qualified candidates. Organizers should communicate clear expectations and evaluation criteria ahead of time, followed by a briefing or calibration session to align scoring standards and ensure consistent, thoughtful reviews.

## Key elements of a successful hackathon judging framework

Hackathon judging criterion define the standards judges use to review and score the projects created during a hackathon. Organizers provide a structured framework that enables the judging panel to evaluate each entry on the same basis and in alignment with the event’s objectives.

Organizers design these benchmarks to reflect the hackathon’s specific purpose, whether the goal is to spark groundbreaking ideas, discover market‑ready solutions, or tackle critical social issues. By setting these expectations in advance, organizers give participants clarity on how their work will be assessed and equip judges with a clear reference point for their decisions. Strong judging criteria guide the selection of winning projects and spotlight the key qualities that drive meaningful innovation and long‑term business value.

## Essential factors to consider in hackathon judging criteria

A well‑designed judging criteria helps ensure that standout projects rise to the top for the right reasons. It gives judges a clear lens to evaluate ideas, balance technical skills, creativity, and real‑world potential. Here are some key factors that often separate the winners from the rest:

- Innovation and originality: The strongest entries bring fresh thinking to the table. These are the projects that surprise you with an unexpected solution, a clever twist on existing tech, or an entirely new way of tackling the challenge. They move ideas forward, rather than simply repeating what’s been done before.

- Technical execution: In a hackathon, time is short, so seeing a well‑built, stable, and efficient solution speaks volumes about a team’s skill and discipline. Clever use of tools, clean architecture, and thoughtful problem-solving are all signs that the project could succeed beyond the event.

- Relevance to the challenge: A brilliant idea loses momentum if it doesn’t address the problem at hand. The most impressive solutions stay rooted in the brief, meeting or exceeding exactly what the challenge asked for while still finding room for creativity.

- User experience: It’s one thing to make something work; it’s another to make it a pleasure to use. Judges should look for solutions that are easy to navigate, visually appealing, and accessible, because great UX often decides whether an idea will make it in the real world.

- Scalability and adaptability: Some prototypes are destined to remain prototypes, while others show they can grow. The ability to handle more users, more data, or different use cases hints that a project has legs beyond the hackathon.

- Impact and value: The best ideas change something for the better; whether that’s adding revenue, streamlining a process, saving costs, or making a real social impact; the more transparent and more tangible the benefit, the stronger the case for the project.

- Clarity of presentation: Even the most innovative ideas can be overlooked if they’re poorly explained. Winning teams know how to tell the story of their project, show why it matters, and demonstrate precisely how it works, all within their short pitch window.

- Team collaboration: Hackathons are a test of working under pressure, and teams that communicate well, delegate effectively, and combine strengths tend to build more rounded, polished solutions. Good teamwork is often reflected in the quality of the final output.

## How Mercer Assessments can help

Mercer Assessments’ Xathon is an all-in-one hackathon management platform that hosts hackathons effortlessly and successfully. Crafted to host large-scale, engaging hackathons, it helps identify and hire top tech talent and engage with existing employees and tech communities. Some of the key features are:

- Real-time and seamless collaboration with stakeholders - mentors, judges, participants and organizers.

- Easy login for mentors and judges to provide insights and access team data and submissions.

- Easy-to-create personalized event pages with a custom registration form to engage participants.

- Quick scheduling of tasks and stages on a dashboard.

- Seamless integration with other tools, internal social networks, and IT systems.

- Simple submission management to ease the process of monitoring scores, submissions, and status.

- Insightful leadership board to receive live event updates on top performers and other crucial aspects.

## What is a Coding Aptitude Test?

A coding aptitude test, also known as a programming aptitude test, is an assessment intended to understand candidates’ knowledge and abilities to utilize the coding skills required to be a competent programmer. The test is designed to help tech recruiters hire entry-level programmers, enabling them to perform a comprehensive evaluation of professionals before making a hiring decision.

Society for Human Resource Management states employers spend an average of US$4,129 on every job hiring in the United States. Despite spending considerable resources, financial and otherwise, companies are unable to find quality talent. Organizations often agreed on hiring the best talent at the time but realized they were either under skilled or unprepared to work within a functional environment. The struggle is real because irrespective of the changes in hiring strategies, most practices remain the same, such as an incomplete or inefficient assessment of a programmer’s aptitude.

Let’s take an example of an aptitude test:

## Introduction

Assessment centers, touted by most as the top-notch hiring and development solution, are designed to measure specific pre-defined competencies that are often mapped to multiple virtual assessment tools for hiring or development purposes. Talent management processes are undergoing a shift as organizations are adapting to a digital way of work. Physical assessment centers are giving way to virtual ones due to their cost, time, and resource efficiency, and quick and easy-to-roll-out features.

## What is a virtual assessment center?

A virtual assessment center, also known as digital assessment center, is a fully online simulation of a traditional assessment center, which replicates real-life workplace situations to evaluate participants’ skills and behaviors in a controlled environment to make crucial decisions about hiring, developing and identifying organizational talent.

Designed to measure multiple skills and competencies for a particular role, virtual assessment centres use personality inventories, cognitive ability tests, situational judgment tests, day-in-the-life situations, role plays, case study simulators, in-basket exercises, caselets, presentations, competency-based interviews, and other such activities, in combination, in the digital format.

As opposed to a physical or traditional assessment center, a virtual or digital assessment center, administered online, optimally utilizes new-age technology to achieve comprehensive and efficient results, without compromising on the credibility and effectiveness of the process. With a complete suite of online tools and technologies, digital assessment centers assist organizations in matching employees to a particular role, defined by a set of competencies. Organizations also identify employees’ strengths and skill gaps required to succeed on the job.

Virtual assessments are mapped to behavioral competencies just as traditional assessment centers. They also contain multiple tools that are administered online with accurate automated reports, eliminating the hassle of logistics and manual efforts. We are using a computerized simulation of specific job-related tasks. It’s a unique pre-employment test that allows the differences to surface in a manner that helps recruiters identify the best-fit candidates for the organization that delivers superior results. We believe that such virtual assessment does more than help the company select the right candidates.

Sophie Summers

HR Manager, RapidAPI.

## Why is an online assessment center a better alternative to a physical centre?

The emergence of virtual assessment centres has enabled us to overcome many challenges faced in traditional assessment centers.

Scalability

Traditional assessment centers come with a limited capacity for participants as well as assessors. A single geographic location is a hindrance to scalability. Online assessment centers enable an unlimited number of participants to perform their best virtually, without the hassle of travel and coordination. Virtual assessment centers enable us to conduct assessments at different locations at the same time, without hampering the quality of the engagement or the results.

Time

The time-taken in a traditional assessment center, starting from scheduling, assessment implementation, analyzing results, providing feedback to making the final decision, can be excruciatingly long, given the multiplicity of factors. Traditional assessment centers can typically take weeks and months due to extensive planning and scheduling constraints. Online assessment centers expedite the process by harnessing technology. Participants can be a part of the virtual assessment center, irrespective of their geographical presence. Given its sole dependence on the internet, the results are immediate, and the execution is simple.

Cost

A traditional assessment center can be expensive, therefore unscalable and limited to a select few employees. Booking a physical center, and managing other logistical requirements, such as arranging for travel, food, and accommodation, and other costs involved in planning a center increases the overhead expenses substantially. However, e-assessment centers can provide a virtual environment with the same level of engagement at a fraction of that cost.

Participant & assessor experience

An e-assessment center enables participation from anywhere, ensuring candidates participate at a time convenient to them so that there’s no wastage of work hours. In a traditional setting, all the participants travel to a central location, which results in not only inflated costs but also the loss of productive hours.

A virtual assessment center is an excellent tool of choice for teams spread across geographies, catering to employees across multiple departments/ functions, of certain seniority, or unwilling to travel. It also reduces the risk of stress affecting the participant’s performance during exercises and assessment, due to travel, and logistical discomfort.

Prone to bias

Physical assessment centers are prone to bias and subtleties of individual assessors. Virtual spaces, on the other hand, are often perceived as more liberating. A virtual assessment center assures a standardized online assessment, with little or no involvement of an assessor, leading to minimum bias, better employee performance, and results. A virtual assessment center ensures a comforting, consistent, and objective environment where participants are safe from confounding or extraneous factors and can carry on with their assessment in a stress-free manner.

One size fits all approach

A holistic understanding of employees is a trademark of the traditional assessment center; one can challenge that it often overlooks employees who might be reserved or introverted. While traditional assessment centers have a one-size-fits-all approach for its employees, virtual assessment centers can be customized to provide a level playing field for all employees, thereby increasing employee satisfaction.

Data & information

Another upside of choosing an online assessment center is that all the activity is happening in the virtual world, which means the piles of paperwork that assessors usually maintain during physical assessment centers and then collate for the final result is eradicable. Online assessment centers facilitate standardization of assessments, easy benchmarking, and easy culling of results. Their ability to produce instant and automated results with minimum or no manual efforts is often a business-puller.

The virtual assessment and development centers are capable of replacing traditional workplace activities and initiatives and they already have replaced the traditional processes in the majority of the businesses. They are of immense help for goal-oriented organizations as then HR professionals have more time to focus on their core competencies. It is best recommended to organizations where high-volume hiring is required.

Sophie Summers

HR Manager, RapidApi

Virtual assessment centers help organizations get better results in a shorter time while ensuring it is a win-win for everyone involved in the execution, participation, and evaluation stages of the process. With technology acting as an enabler, an online assessment center allows organizations to extend opportunities of growth to all their employees in a streamlined manner.

## Why should you shift to a virtual assessment center?

As the global economy evolves and organizations encourage remote work, professionals are looking up to their employers, not just to instill a sense of security, but also to keep them motivated during unprecedented times.

The post-COVID-19 era has already pushed employees to take up skills initially taken for granted – interpersonal communication, stakeholder management, problem-solving, decision-making, leadership, agility, etc. While entering uncharted territories and striving for future-readiness, employees continue to upskill and reskill themselves naturally. Organizations need to match this skilling speed and need with future-ready strategies.

We will be moving all of our mentoring/training initiatives online. It just makes more sense to do it that way as it's easier to coordinate and can be recorded for posterity. In the case of continued education, online classes will greatly benefit our employees without putting them at risk in a physical classroom setting.

Jennifer Walden

Director of Operations, WikiLawn

Embracing technology in trying times can help boost an organization’s initiatives involving learning and development, high potential identification, leadership development, succession planning, and/or training needs identification.

If your organization had already planned workforce optimization and development, the pandemic is no reason to halt or defer them. There is, in fact, no better time to take these up and strive toward future-proofing your workforce. If a traditional or blended assessment center was your tool of choice, then transitioning to an online assessment center is a smart choice to make during the present business environment. It shows your employees your continued and proactive interest in their development, irrespective of any global crisis.

Remote work is the new normal and many SaaS companies like ourselves had already adapted to the idea of agile working, where borders or where you work from becomes irrelevant...As far as learning and development goes, our learning center has moved online, and since the crisis, we have introduced aspirational objective and key results as well where employees can add to their tasks voluntarily and choose to take courses online paid for by the company for continuous learning.

Shayan Fatani

Digital Marketing Strategist, PureVPN

## How to use online assessment centers for business continuity in a remote work scenario?

Competencies are the fundamental building blocks of any assessment and development center. To holistically assess the personality, cognitive and behavioral competencies and paint a complete picture of an individual, the need for more than one tool is a generally accepted premise. Hence, a virtual assessment center measures each competency through two or more tools, optimally utilizing the available time and resources, and striving toward future-proofing your workforce.

Identification of High Potential Employees

HiPo employees are considered exceptional contributors to the future growth of a business. A well-thought-out high potential program implemented through a comprehensive online assessment center can ensure that identified talent gets access and time to assimilate new skills in an objective and cost-effective manner, positively affecting the bottom line, which is a pressing need of the hour for many organizations.

As remote work becomes a norm, many organizations are building internal teams to meet specific needs of such a scenario. A high potential identification initiative led through a virtual assessment center can fulfil the said specific needs.

If, for instance, your organization is looking to measure innovation to address current business challenges in a high potential employee, a combination of a personality profiler, cognitive ability test, and case study simulator can easily help you evaluate this competency.

Leadership Development & Succession Planning

With the unpredictable nature of changing work cultures, organizations are truly acknowledging the value of good leadership skills to successfully traverse through uncharted territories while relentlessly striving to keep their teams engaged and motivated. The current market scenario, given its volatility, uncertainty, and competitiveness, demands future-proofing your business. Leaders are the backbone of any organization. Hence, it is essential for an organization to be future-ready and have a systematically identified talent pipeline that can be developed to take up more demanding roles and responsibilities and deal with complex future challenges. An e-assessment center can help businesses identify future leaders effective in the age of digital transformation and develop a structured and efficient succession plan.

For example, your organization is looking for competencies such as planning and organization, data-driven decision making, complex problem solving, strategic thinking, people development, etc. in the future leaders of the company. A virtual assessment center can come to your rescue with exercises like inbox prioritization, situational judgement tests, and case study simulator-that measure these competencies in an objective and unbiased virtual environment.

Training Needs Identification for L&D Initiatives

A critical strategy for future-readiness is to identify the skill gaps in your workforce and creating engaging learning and development opportunities for your employees. Often these processes are sidelined due to other pressing business needs. But with organizations striving to find a fine balance between meeting business targets and motivating their employees to stay on track, these initiatives can increase the levels of commitment and engagement in an employee, thereby leading to an increased level of satisfaction, better productivity, or better still, a decrease in employee attrition rate.

Without a doubt, more L&D initiatives can be moved online. Any organization that is not considering shifting learning modes online is living in the past and missing out on major efficiency gains, coupled with opportunities to increase the satisfaction and loyalty of the workforce. Access to development opportunities is a critical determinant in employee engagement and commitment.

Jeff Skipper

Owner & CEO, Jeff Skipper Consulting

An organization’s proactive contribution to talent development makes employees appreciate them more. In addition to loyalty and gratitude, employees feel closer to the broader business vision, especially at a critical juncture like this, when everyone is feeling alienated working in silos.

We understand that employees hate to be stuck in a rut and are hungry for knowledge, especially now when we're all hemmed in at home and looking for ways to spend time productively. We devote every ounce of our energy to help employees grow professionally….with virtual mentorship opportunities...and online skilling courses and webinars, so they could devour knowledge and ultimately help our company reach its true North once the pandemic subsides. I think it's important to continually emphasize that, as a company, you're committed to helping employees grow their muscles. Otherwise, they are more likely to lose steam and eventually look for greener pastures.

Jagoda Wieczorek

HR Manager, ResumeLab

## Top 7 exercises that ensure a holistic virtual assessment

A typical virtual assessment center includes several methods of evaluation. While these methods may be different for every company or situation, there are several common exercises that help boost the efficiency of a VAC. Let’s dive into the top five.

### 1. Psychometric assessment

Various types of psychometric assessments are used to measure a candidate’s role-specific potential, industry-specific aptitude, personality traits, and other essential qualities. Various question formats are used for such an analysis depending on the goal of the assessment center process.

### 2. Virtual assessment center group exercises

Virtual assessment center group exercise examples include group discussions and problem-solving as a team. They revolve around observing candidates and their abilities to collaborate with other people. There is a brief given and time-limit set for this exercise. Participants get the chance to demonstrate skills like reasoning, creativity, proactiveness, memory, social engagement, and public speaking.

### 3. Competency-based interview

Competency-based interviews take traditional job interviews to the virtual space. Questions asked in these interviews are chosen to understand the candidate’s industry knowledge, skill level, experience, etc. Results and selection are based on competency-focused interactions among candidates and interviewers.

### 4. Case study analysis

A VAC case study provides the candidates with a set of documents highlighting detailed information about real-life industry-specific situations. The candidate is required to interpret this information and come up with insightful analyses, plans of action, data, as a way to highlight their findings.

### 5. Roleplays

Roleplay exercises are designed to evaluate a candidate’s interpersonal skills, negotiation prowess, communication abilities, and the knack to influence decisions in a logical, fact-based manner. These exercises can include elaborate discussions in mock professional scenarios where candidates may be asked to assume relevant professional roles.

### 6. Inbox exercises

Inbox exercises are classic assessment center activities designed to evaluate the candidate’s ability to prioritize multiple tasks and deal with challenges at work. It’s mostly related to sorting emails and working on quick projects within a short duration.

### 7. Situational judgement test

A situational judgement test, also known as an SJT, primarily involves multiple choice questions for testing a candidate’s ability to deal with real-life work-related situations. SJTs are a cost-effective and powerful tool for selecting strong professionals who can perform well in specific roles.

## What to expect, how to succeed, and how to prepare for a virtual assessment center?

## Tips for candidates

Candidates who have been a part of ACDCs (assessment center development center), will find it relatively easy to transition to a virtual assessment center. Once you have a fair idea of various virtual assessment center exercises, tools, and virtual assessment center ideas, you can begin preparing in a more focused way.

In this section, we enlist the top ten tips that will help you succeed in a virtual assessment center.

### 1. Understand the basics

Before you appear at a virtual assessment center, it is crucial to know what to expect. Usually, it takes 2-3 hours for all VAC activities to complete. In addition, there could be specific tech requirements like setting up a webcam and microphone, accommodating tech installation settings in your system, etc. The more you learn about these details in advance, the better would be your preparedness on the big day.

### 2. Brush up your digital fluency

You may be required to switch screens and browse through various types of digital tools and virtual assessment center examples. Therefore, digital fluency becomes essential for success in a virtual assessment center. Your speed should be adequate without causing you to feel overwhelmed or anxious.

### 3. Familiarize yourself with key VAC components

In addition to basic digital fluency, it always helps when you are acquainted with the types of virtual assessment center platforms you would be introduced to during VAC exercises. While this guide gives you detailed insights into VACs, we recommend discussing the same with your organization to have a clearer understanding of what to expect.

### 4. Virtual assessment center practice!

As stated earlier in this blog, virtual assessment centers include complex assessments for aptitude, competencies, behaviors, and so on. Moreover, there are professional activities like case studies and presentations for which you should be well prepared.

### 5. Stay updated

Other than current affairs, it is vital to be aware of developments and trends specific to your industry and job profile. You should be confident about everything you say and write during a virtual assessment. And that kind of confidence comes from being updated with the most important highlights, data, statistics, and actionable recommendations from leaders and experts in your niche.

### 6. Ensure you are connected to a stable network

Virtual assessment centers are extensive and you cannot afford to deal with a fluctuating WIFI or malfunctioning network. A strong and stable internet connectivity is one of the top necessities if you want to succeed in a virtual assessment center.

### 7. Test your system and equipment for technical glitches

In tune with the previous point, you should also ensure that your computer and additional equipment are functioning smoothly. It is always recommended that you test everything a couple of times before the assessment day.

### 8. Be confident and dress well

You may be required to appear for a virtual face-to-face round during interviews, group discussions, and other activities. Therefore, formal attire is one of the simplest ways to ensure you feel confident and at the top of your game.

### 9. Make a checklist

Making a list of things to do and practice before a virtual assessment session can be a huge help in taking away the jitters. It also helps remember every detail that is important to you. That way, you can enter a virtual assessment center feeling stress-free and less overwhelmed.

### 10. Be and active listener to be an active contributor

This is a key advice for candidates taking part in group discussions. Any type of group activity requires presence of mind, patience, and professionalism. Always remember the competencies that a group activity measures: ability to work in a team, interpersonal skills, problem solving qualities, etc. To be able to check all those boxes for the assessors, you need to prove that you are a good listener as well as an active contributor.

### Conclusion
