## Frequently asked questions (FAQs)

###

Online remote proctoring is a method of overseeing examinations conducted over the Internet. It employs technology to monitor test-takers in real time, ensuring exam security and integrity while allowing students to take assessments from remote locations.

###

Online proctored test work by monitoring test-takers' screens. The test takers must switch on their video and audio to verify their identity. They cannot start the exam before validating their ID. After the approval, the remote proctored exam begins, and an AI and/or a human proctor monitors the exam from start to finish. During the test, an ideal proctoring software monitors test-takers' screen activity, locks down web browsers, and enables the flagging of suspicious activities to prevent malpractices.

###

Yes, online proctoring often involves recording the screen to monitor exam activity and reduce instances of cheating. The proctoring software captures students’ screens alongside webcam and audio feeds during the exam.

###

Online test monitoring does not have the capability to detect other devices directly. However, it can monitor network activity, require the test-taker to use a specific browser, and utilize dual camera proctoring for a 360-degree view.

###

The three main types of proctored exams are:

  • Live online proctoring with a human invigilator monitoring candidates' screens in real-time.
  • Recorded online proctoring with AI monitoring, later reviewed by human proctors.
  • Advanced online proctoring without any human intervention, where advanced AI monitors and flags suspicious activities to score candidate integrity.

###

An online proctored exam utilizes technology and proctors to monitor the test-takers' screen activities. These examinations may have a human invigilator remotely supervising the test. A non-proctored exam is unsupervised and allows test takers to complete the test at their chosen time and pace. For this reason, remote proctoring ensures greater reliability and integrity in the test-taking and evaluation process compared to non-proctored exams.

###

In hybrid proctoring, the automated system flags suspicious behavior and the human proctor who reviews those flags and intervenes when needed.

##

Hiring managers often face challenges in effectively evaluating job candidates without a data-driven approach. Traditional methods like resumes and interviews can be unreliable, as many resumes lack authenticity, and interviews may not yield relevant insights into a candidate’s potential success. In order to improve recruitment processes, assessments are essential as they evaluate candidates’ abilities, aptitudes, and personalities. Online assessments, conducted through web-based technologies, offer an efficient solution, providing valuable data for informed hiring decisions.

This blog will detail the intricacies of online assessment, its types, benefits, use cases and how organizations can find the right online assessment software for their talent hiring and management needs.

## What is an online assessment?

Online assessment refers to the administration of tests via digital platforms to evaluate participants’ learning and proficiency in specific subjects. These assessments are designed to measure candidates’ skills, knowledge, and competencies relevant to various roles, using a range of formats including numerical reasoning, logical thinking, and personality evaluations. The evaluations typically consist of structured questions aimed at objectively assessing an individual’s capabilities and predicting job performance.

## Types of online assessments

Psychometric assessments

Psychometric assessments are assessment tools to evaluate a person’s competencies, behavior and aptitude. They are designed to assess personality traits and role fitment. They measure how individual behavior affects workplace dynamics and vice-versa. Employers then use the information gauged via psychometric assessment tests to make informed hiring decisions. They are divided into two categories:

Personality assessments

A personality test is a systematic evaluation of human personality constructs. It is commonly used as a part of the pre-employment assessment process. The employer administers these tests to assess a candidate’s personality characteristics. The tests measure how an applicant’s personality traits correlate to work performance.

Personality assessments are based on the premise that observable changes in an individual’s behavior vary from person to person based on underlying traits. The traits may differ in people from different socio-economic backgrounds, cultures, religious beliefs, and upbringings. Personality assessments aim to measure these traits objectively. They can be administered to observe a change in personality, screen job applicants and provide a holistic view of an individual’s weaknesses or strengths.

Some personality assessments offered by Mercer | Mettl are:

- Mercer | Mettl Personality Map: Measures key personality traits and behavioral competencies for senior roles and job profiles.

- Mercer | Mettl Motivation Inventory: Assesses a candidate’s key motivators to continue working in a particular company or industry.

- Mercer | Mettl Learning Agility Assessment: A scientifically validated tool that assesses the capabilities of high learning-agile individuals.

Cognitive assessments

Cognitive assessments measure an individual’s cognitive skills, such as critical thinking, verbal reasoning, numerical ability, problem-solving, decision-making, etc. The test results indicate on-the-job performance and assess potential employees across job levels. These online tests also measure role-specific IQs across multiple job functions.

Cognitive tests play a critical role in mapping the workforce’s development journey. They reveal the competency gaps on which employees need to be trained to perform better. They also help HR improve the quality of hires. Cognitive tests can correctly predict the probability of success in almost any job – from beginner to executive level. Such assessments include questions to assess candidates’ potential to use cognitive abilities to solve complex problems or acquire new knowledge.

Some cognitive assessments offered by Mercer | Mettl are:

- Mercer | Mettl Cognitive Abilities Assessment: Evaluates an individual’s abstract thinking skills, the ability to grasp complex concepts and make rational inferences.

- Logical Reasoning Test: Assesses a candidate’s reasoning abilities and ability to analyze information from various perspectives and derive conclusions.

- Cognitive Speed Test: Measures a candidate’s spatial reasoning, verbal ability, and math and logic skills.

Technical assessments

While psychometric assessments assess human personality, traits, behavior, and intelligence, technical assessments focus on an individual’s subject matter expertise in their line of work. They test the in-depth knowledge of the person. The questions in a technical evaluation are based on the skill requirement of that particular role. The competencies in technical assessment vary with the job role, job function and industry. To hire the most competent tech professionals, employers use technical assessments to assess aspirants’ knowledge across skills and subskills. The specific skills and proficiency for a particular job role are quickly evaluated through the technical assessment test. By conducting a technical exam, recruiters can determine if candidates have the suitable expertise required for a given position.

Technical assessments can be divided into three categories:

Coding assessments

Online coding assessments are automated, structured frameworks to assess candidates’ coding skills in a dedicated programming environment. These tests enable recruiting and engineering teams to conduct pre-employment screening for programming roles effectively at a large scale. Employers use coding tests to gain insight into applicants’ skills and abilities.

Online coding assessments encompass numerous coding skills. These assessments include a C developer test, Java developer test, C++ developer assessment, software testing, python development, and more. Coding tests assess prospects on various languages and technologies within real coding environments, such as Java Spring, ReactJS, C#, automation testing, Oracle DBA, SQL, and much more. These tests evaluate the output and consider numerous parameters such as code, time and space complexity.

Some coding assessments offered by Mercer | Mettl are:

- Core Java Developer Assessment: Assesses a candidate’s skills, knowledge, and conceptual understanding of Java.

- Front-end Developer Test: Evaluates a front-end developer’s technical skills, knowledge, and abilities with an emphasis on practical coding skills.

- Back-end Developer Assessment: Measures a candidate’s programming skills and knowledge to develop or enhance existing applications, identifying potential hires by assessing their skills and job readiness.

Role-based assessments

Role-based assessments, or domain skills assessments, are suitable for gauging the job-specific skills of applicants. Recruiters can assess job seekers’ competencies with the expert-curated problems provided in these assessments. The purpose of role-based evaluations is to determine the domain expertise of individuals. This test enables hiring managers to onboard the most eligible candidate.

Role-based assessments are customized for various job functions such as marketing, sales, finance, operations, customer support, etc. These tests are also used to re-skill employees to enhance workforce productivity. The assessment results shed light on the areas needing improvement, which helps prepare personalized training programs for workforce development per industry criteria.

Some role-based assessments offered by Mercer | Mettl are:

- Mercer | Mettl Leadership Assessment: Assesses the candidate’s competencies required for a leadership role.

- Assessment for Business Analysts: Evaluates a candidate’s business acumen, cognitive competencies, and ability to understand, comprehend, analyze and solve business problems.

- Mercer | Mettl Channel Sales Executive Assessment: Assesses a candidate’s leadership qualities, sales aptitude and interpersonal skills.

Communication proficiency assessments

A communication proficiency test measures an individual’s fluency, pronunciation, grammar and comprehension skills. It plays a crucial role in effective communication. This pre-employment test acts as a filtration tool that screens out unsuitable candidates and helps employers find candidates with excellent oral and written skills.

The communication test accurately assesses a person’s language skills, whether writing, speaking or listening. These tests provide crucial information on both job candidates’ and employees’ ability to use the language to comprehend and communicate thoughts, ideas, and issues.

Some communication proficiency assessments offered by Mercer | Mettl are:

- SpeechX: Evaluates candidates on four aspects of the English language, i.e., pronunciation, fluency, grammar and listening comprehension.

- English Reading Comprehension Test: Assesses whether the test-taker can process textual information, understand its essence and draw logical conclusions.

- Writing Skills Assessment: Assesses candidates’ ability to present ideas through written text.

Online tests include various question types, such as multiple choice, coding, multiple-response, true/false, audio response, project or case study-based, and subjective or essay-type questions.

## 2. Online assessments for organizational development purposes

Learning and development

Employee learning and development directly impact revenue, cost and overall productivity. The change and churn are making numerous job profiles obsolete. A majority of organizations have frozen their ongoing recruitment. The focus of businesses has now shifted to sustenance, employee engagement and development. Organizations must continue investing in employee training with a host of upcoming skills and technologies in demand.

The current situation demands employees to upskill and cross-skill to stay relevant. To meet these requirements, employers must first identify their workforce’s training needs by utilizing the pre-training assessment, followed by skill gaps identification and a development plan based on the assessment report. Employers can then analyze the training effectiveness via a post-training evaluation, which helps map employees’ development journey.

High-potential identification

A high potential (HiPo) is an employee with all the traits and attributes required to climb the corporate ladder, assume new roles and responsibilities, and undertake more advanced challenges. HiPos are distinctly recognized among their peers in the organization. They are crucial for driving business performance and achieving better productivity and profit. They demonstrate skills and qualities that align with the organization’s culture and vision. High-potential identification is a process that discovers individuals with high potential to undertake new organizational and personal advancement roles.

Despite being crucial, conducting the HiPo process is a challenging affair. For this purpose, a scientifically validated battery of online assessments is handy. Such reviews can be customized easily to measure talent potential without fail.

Succession planning

Organizations need a skilled and experienced leader to navigate the post-COVID-19 turbulence, someone with a deep understanding of effective crisis management, workplace disruption and problem-solving. However, to build a leadership pipeline, businesses must first identify the high-potential (HiPo) employees with the knowledge, expertise and potential to take up future leadership roles.

When organizations commit to succession planning, they build a leadership pipeline that develops high-potential talent, keeping those team members invested and on track for future success.

Jill Pioter

Director of Branding and Communication, Psychological Associates.

Online succession planning tools play a significant role in identifying and developing high-potential employees. Unlike subjective leadership evaluation, online assessments objectively evaluate competencies, skills, and behaviors critical for leadership positions.

Effective succession planning provides:

- Improved retention of HiPos

- Increased availability of skilled leaders

- Planning of career paths

## 3. Online assessments in education

Online assessment in education is a critical component that significantly impacts the holistic learning structure. Online educational evaluation systematically chronicles and utilizes empirical data on candidates’ skills and course-based subject knowledge. This assessment method helps teachers align the learning outcomes with teaching methodology to encourage a more effective learning process. Assessments are an impartial analysis of an individual learner or all individuals collectively.

There are eight different types of assessments of learning:

- Formative: A formative assessment is aimed at monitoring students’ learning and providing ongoing feedback that enhances the learning process’s efficacy.

- Summative: A summative assessment measures students’ learning at the end of an instructive unit.

- Diagnostic: A diagnostic assessment is administered at the start to assess candidates’ prior knowledge to understand their knowledge level, skills, strengths, and weaknesses.

- Confirmative: A confirmative assessment aims to determine whether the learning imparted by instructors is still effective after a year of training.

- Norm-referenced: A norm-referenced assessment compares a candidate's performance against an average norm, meaning a relative performance comparison of a student with other students.

- Criterion-referenced: A criterion-referenced assessment evaluates a student's performance against predetermined learning criteria, meaning it assesses what learners are expected to know at a particular stage of their education.

- Benchmark: A benchmark assessment is conducted periodically to evaluate the student's performance and is mainly carried out at the end of a grading period.

- Ipsative: An ipsative assessment aims to understand students' progress by assessing their current performance against previous performances.

## What are the types of questions asked during assessments?

There are a wide range of questions asked during an online test. Some of them are:

- Multiple choice questions: In this type, the candidate must choose one option from the available options.

- Coding questions: These questions are asked to comprehend a person’s understanding of various coding languages such as Java, C++, Python, and SQL.

- Multi-response questions: Here, a candidate can choose multiple options they feel are suitable.

- True and false questions: Candidates must pick whether it is false or true according to the statement given in the question.

- Audio response questions: The candidate must hear the sound clip in them first. It is followed by questions based on it.

- Project and case study-based questions: Project and case study-based questions are constructed to get clarity about a candidate in the field. These questions may include a topic, the company, or the project case study.

- Subjective and essay-type questions: In these questions, candidates can express their opinions freely. These questions are beneficial in knowing the character and values of candidates.

## Top benefits of online assessments

Traditional recruitment methods are not free from limitations. Online assessment tools have the edge over their retro counterparts when evaluating candidates’ capabilities holistically. The ample leeway these assessments have over their predecessors is the accuracy and flexibility they offer to recruiters in various talent verticals and screen out misfits from the cohort early in the process. They justify evaluating, analyzing and documenting the test-takers’ work readiness, training needs, learning progress, and skill acquisition. The benefits of online assessments are substantial, some of which are listed below:

- Better candidate selection

Online assessments measure candidates’ capabilities and gather essential data on their skills, abilities, and personalities. The test can help ascertain whether they are a good fit for organizations. These assessments are proctored online with the highest security standards. Therefore, the integrity of these tests is unwavering. Online assessments are normative, which helps employers conduct an objective and fair evaluation of candidates to determine the right person for the role. Since these tests have inherent scientific reliability, their results can be valid indicators for the prospective candidate’s future job performance.

- Data-driven hiring decisions

Online assessment analytics lend unparalleled ease to dissect complex data to furnish crucial insights, enabling employers to make data-driven hiring decisions. With instant test results and report generation in real-time, the candidate evaluation report gets generated as soon as the test-taker completes the online assessment. Since online reviews make it incredibly easy to test thousands of candidates, they help recruiters build a sizable talent repository, which is helpful for future hiring. Moreover, hiring managers can leverage the power of insightful data generated from assessing so many candidates.

- Better filtration in campus hiring

Online assessments can help companies identify prospective hires during a campus hiring drive. By utilizing these tools, recruiters can save a significant amount of time by not having to administer tests for every candidate manually and single-handedly but rather automating the entire process with the help of online assessments. These tests are an excellent filtration tool to assess a large applicant pool, screen out unsuitable applicants and qualify top talent. These assessment tests are used as standard pre-recruitment tools to assess various skills (both hard and soft) for technical and non-technical roles. Additionally, one can employ specific online assessments such as psychometric tests, culture fit tests, aptitude tests, and behavioral tests to obtain a holistic profile of candidates.

- Assessing cultural fit

Online assessments are also helpful when understanding a candidate’s cultural fit during the hiring process. Cultural fit is the congruity of beliefs, values, and objectives between the employer and employee. When a candidate aligns perfectly with an organization’s values and goals, it might be translated into a successful long-term relationship. A cultural fit assessment helps employers determine what would matter to prospective employees once they start working at an organization. The test is a helpful tool to assess candidates’ cultural fit and increase retention rate by selecting candidates who are the best fit for the company.

- Scalability

With the advent of online assessments came the convenience of reaching beyond the constraints of geographical limitations. Now, examining bodies can reach out to candidates from far-flung areas, unlike before when administering tests was limited to physical test centers.

- Easy accessibility

Examinees nowadays prefer working on a computer and are not keen on adopting the traditional pen-and-paper approach. Candidates are so used to computer editing tools while writing that they cannot do without them; for example, copying and pasting text and using spreadsheets have become commonplace tasks. Switching to pen and paper would be toilsome when they have become accustomed to working digitally.

- Minimized administrative burden

By turning to online assessments, evaluators significantly reduce administrative hassles such as organizing and conducting exams. Printing and distributing estimates on paper and organizing the supplies of complete scripts for evaluation purposes is tedious.

- Enhanced security

Security concerns are appropriately addressed in an online test setting, where all test papers, candidate details, and grades are digitally available. Besides, the security level is remarkably high because only authorized people can access the assessment.

- Flexibility

Online assessments offer unparalleled ease of taking exams from anywhere. Features such as online remote proctoring enable examinees to take an exam from the comfort of their homes securely and conveniently.

- In-depth reports

Online assessment reports are comprehensive and provide insights into candidates’ results and progress. Such a report delves deep into how candidates perform in a particular area and which areas require immediate attention.

- Auto-grading

Online assessments can simplify the evaluation process and provide test outcomes much faster than traditional assessments. With the auto-grading feature, assessors spend less time grading manually and give the candidates immediate feedback.

- Collaborative authoring

In the case of an online assessment, authoring questions becomes a collaborative process. The examining body can easily manage the tasks while creating questions because transparent workflows are defined for reviewing and selecting problems before including them in the question bank.

- Cost-effectiveness

Administering online assessments is cost-effective because administrators save time and resources while performing administrative operations, including exam creation, delivery and circulation, and evaluation processes.

- Accommodates candidates with disabilities

Administrators can conduct online assessments even for candidates with disabilities. It is easier to change the background color, font size, etc. Moreover, the test format perfectly caters to those candidates with special considerations.

## How do online assessments work

Online assessment tools evaluate knowledge, skills, abilities, and even personality traits in a digital environment. The process is designed to be scalable, secure, and efficient, making it suitable for everything from campus hiring to leadership development.

At the heart of an online assessment is a digital platform that hosts the test. Candidates can log in from anywhere, using a secure browser or platform that often comes with built-in measures to prevent cheating, such as AI-based proctoring, webcam monitoring, and browser lockdowns. These tests can be objective (like multiple-choice questions) or subjective (like essay-based answers or coding simulators).

Once a candidate completes the test, the responses are automatically evaluated based on pre-set scoring algorithms or human review in more complex assessments. This not only speeds up decision-making but also removes the bias and logistical constraints of traditional evaluations.

The real strength of online assessments lies in their ability to generate data, providing insights into how someone thinks, solves problems, or fits a role. This data can be used to benchmark against role requirements, build skill profiles, or even tailor learning paths for development.

## Use cases of online assessments

Online assessments are no longer limited to exams in educational settings. Organizations across sectors use them to solve diverse hiring, training, and talent management challenges. Here are some key use cases:

### 1. Recruitment and hiring

Organizations use online assessments to screen candidates for cognitive ability, job-specific skills, or behavioral fit. This ensures that only the most qualified applicants move forward, saving time and improving the quality of hire.

### 2. Campus hiring at scale

For companies hiring from multiple universities, online assessments standardize the evaluation process. They enable companies to reach thousands of students across geographies without logistical challenges.

### 3. Learning and development

Assessments help identify current skill levels and tailor upskilling programs accordingly. They ensure that L&D efforts are data-backed and personalized, from technical training to leadership development.

### 4. Internal mobility and succession planning

Assessments help find high-potential employees, evaluate readiness for new roles, and create career paths based on skill data, not just tenure.

### 5. Certification and compliance

Industries like finance and healthcare use assessments to certify professionals on regulatory or technical knowledge, ensuring compliance and competence in high-stakes environments.

## How to choose the best online assessment software for pre-employment assessments

Choosing an online assessment platform is about finding a solution that aligns with your hiring or learning objectives, scales with your needs, and offers a reliable, user-friendly experience for all stakeholders involved. Here’s what to consider:

### 1. Flexibility in assessment design

The right platform should allow you to evaluate a wide variety of skills—from technical and cognitive to behavioral and domain-specific—with minimal setup. Many leading platforms offer extensive libraries of pre-built assessments that can be easily customized.

For instance, Mercer | Mettl provides role-based assessments mapped to industry benchmarks, making it easier to hit the ground running with minimal manual effort. Furthermore, Mercer | Mettl also allows organizations to customize assessments as per their needs.

### 2. Built-in proctoring and test integrity tools

Maintaining test integrity in remote settings is critical. Look for platforms that combine AI-based proctoring with human invigilation, along with features like secure browsers, candidate authentication, and real-time alerts.

The Mercer | Mettl online assessment platform offers a layered approach to proctoring, combining facial recognition, browser lockdown through MSB, and even live proctors. This ensures the highest levels of test integrity.

### 3. Seamless candidate experience

A smooth user experience can make or break your assessment strategy. From easy access and intuitive navigation to multilingual support and compatibility with various devices, candidate-first design is key.

Platforms like Mercer | Mettl are optimized for low-bandwidth environments and mobile responsiveness, making them particularly useful for large-scale hiring or geographically distributed teams.

### 4. Analytics that go beyond scores

Raw scores are helpful, but actionable insights are game-changing. The best platforms provide analytics dashboards that break down performance by skills, offer benchmarking, and even give behavioral insights.

### 5. Integration with your HR ecosystem

Assessment platforms shouldn’t operate in isolation. Look for options that integrate smoothly with your ATS, LMS, or HRMS, so assessment data flows naturally into your broader talent workflow.

For instance, the Mercer | Mettl online assessment platform offers robust APIs and native integrations with leading HR tech platforms, helping reduce manual handoffs and improving operational efficiency.

Ultimately, the best online assessment platform is one that quietly does the heavy lifting, bringing together scientific rigor, smart technology, and a seamless experience. Mercer| Mettl, which has partnered with corporates across 100+ countries, is among the few platforms that balance all three. This makes it a trusted partner for organizations looking to assess, develop, and transform talent with confidence.

## Introduction

A hackathon is a time-bound competition where teams or individuals try to find solutions to technology-related situations or problems. The event centers on one idea, theme, or problem, and participants try to develop and present a solution or product as a working prototype. A panel of expert judges evaluates the solution to declare a winner based on specific pre-defined parameters.

Initially, hackathons were conducted onsite and focused only on coders. However, with changing times, hackathons have gone virtual, increasing their accessibility and popularity. These events now focus on different issues and use cases related to technologies or programming languages.

## Types of hackathons

Depending on the objectives, hackathons can be organized internally or made open to the public.

Internal hackathons

A company conducts an internal hackathon for its employees. It aims to crowdsource ideas, promote collaboration, and increase employee engagement. Here, companies can involve employees from different backgrounds and give them the freedom to develop innovative ideas that can be pitched to senior management.

External hackathons

External hackathons are open to the public. Anybody, both within and outside the organization, can participate. The participants are usually attracted by the theme and the prize on offer. Virtual external hackathons allow companies to crowdsource ideas from across the world.

Hackathons can also be categorized as:

- Coding competition: The goal is to create software within the assigned time. These hackathons can last from one to three weeks.

- Language-based hackathons: These hackathons aim to create an application based on a specific programming language.

- Industry-based hackathons: Such hackathons are organized to drive innovation in specific industries.

## Benefits of a virtual hackathon

### Economical execution

Onsite hackathons are costly, ranging from renting a place for the event to taking care of participants’ needs. There is also the cost of hiring staff to organize and run the event efficiently.

A virtual hackathon allows most people to participate from their homes, eliminating the need to rent space and arrange food and accommodation. Businesses may need to hire extra staff to monitor the participants, but the number of temporary hires would still be less than onsite hackathons, which makes virtual hackathons economical.

### Increased participation

Physical hackathons limit participation to those near the venue or people who can travel. This means contestants are primarily local. With virtual hackathons, people from all over the world can join. Only a stable internet connection and a device to work on are needed. With people joining from all over the world, businesses have increased chances of receiving a working solution and finding top talent.

### Enhanced participant experience

Everybody has different conditions under which they work better. For example, some candidates might prefer working from the comfort of their homes. Virtual hackathons allow each participant to work in conditions where they are most comfortable working. This directly contributes to increased productivity and improved results.

### Better collaboration

The intensity of trying to find a solution in a set time frame breaks the monotony of day-to-day functions. Hackathons also encourage collaboration and creativity among the team members in a fun environment. This is especially true when members are connecting virtually. They will need to communicate and delegate tasks efficiently, which builds camaraderie.

## Reasons to organize a hackathon

- Crowdsourcing ideas from employees

- Identifying training needs and promoting L&D

- Recognizing high-potential employees

- Identifying and attracting top talent

- Promoting a new product

## How to organize a virtual hackathon?

Despite being virtual, organizing a hackathon is challenging. Here are the three essentials to hosting a successful hackathon.

The prize

Be it an onsite or virtual hackathon, prizes are essential for boosting participation. Rewards can range from cash and gift cards to an internship with the organization or a permanent position. Awards can also depend on the target audience, like software licenses, which help attract tech professionals.

The software

To host your hackathon, choose a platform with robust capabilities. It should have optimum features, the ability to handle the size of the event, and a platform for participants to engage with others. Also, the software provider should have excellent tech support in the case of technical glitches.

The judges

A panel of qualified judges is necessary for the event’s credibility, as participants know they will be evaluated by experts in their field. Well-known judges will also attract top talent and help boost the virtual hackathon's popularity.

## Steps for hosting a virtual hackathon

Decide a goal: The why of your hackathon

Before organizing a hackathon, businesses must decide the reasons behind holding the event. What does the business want out of it? Does the business intend to use it as a marketing campaign? Is the business looking to check the security features of an upcoming app or software? The hackathon idea will set the tone for the planning process and help attract the right audience.

Decide the other four w’s

Deciding the goal takes care of the ‘why’ of the hackathon. But the other four – who, what, where, and when are also important. Here is everything to know:

- Who: ‘Who’ defines the target audience. These are the people who will be participating in the virtual hackathon. To increase participation and maximize the audience, select judges and guest speakers that appeal to the target audience.

- What: It refers to the prizes and incentives offered to winners and participants.

- Where: In the case of onsite hackathons, this is the place where the event will take place. But in the case of online hackathons, it is choosing a platform that meets business and contestants’ needs.

- When: Choosing a date for a virtual event is vital to ensure maximum participation. Avoid major holidays or events in the region or countries where you wish to attract people from. Also, factor in different time zones when planning the event.

Promote the event

After deciding on the virtual hackathon’s theme, prize, judges, and guest speaker, it is essential to spread the word about the hackathon to encourage the target audience to register for the event. Start promoting it on the company website and social media pages and include it in email marketing campaigns. Additionally, posting about it in relevant online communities is another excellent way to promote the hackathon.

Streamline registration

Virtual hackathons tend to attract more participants than onsite ones, which makes it essential that the registration process is easy and streamlined. It would be best to clarify the cutoff dates for registration and put a cap on the number of participants. All of this will help you manage the event effectively.

Include some fun activities

Online interactions are different from offline ones. This makes it important for the business to provide opportunities for participant engagement in a fun and casual way. Such events encourage connection and improve participants’ experience.

Take stock post-event

Post-event analysis is critical to capitalize on things that worked in favor and find the ones that didn’t. Ask participants to provide feedback through a survey form or informally ask them about their experience. This will help the business get better insights for event hosting the next time.

Finally, remember to promote the success of the hackathon through post-event promotions. Share images and videos from the event with key audiences via social media posts, newsletters, and blogs.

## Things to avoid when hosting a hackathon

### Miscommunication in promotion

From the beginning, any promotional posts about the hackathon must be clear and concise. If the hackathon’s advertisement or newsletter is not clear, it will confuse the target audience, bringing down the number of participants.

The easiest way to avoid such a situation is to have a clear goal before communications begin. Businesses can also have a separate events page for FAQs that address common questions.

## Not choosing the right platform

The hackathon platform chosen can help execute the event successfully. ‍Select a platform that works well for the business and participants.

A platform that offers tools for collaboration among participants, easy access to attendees’ information, and the ability to assign scores for the organizers is ideal.

## No incentives or prizes for participants

A hackathon is a competition, and the winning team is entitled to an award decided in advance. However, what about other participants? Lack of recognition can reduce motivation among the attendees and cause participation to drop the next time the event is organized.

To avoid this scenario, deciding on a participation prize is ideal. The goodies could be the organization’s promotional items or limited access to a product’s full features. Remember to communicate the same when promoting hackathon to draw more people.

## How Mercer | Mettl can help

Mercer | Mettl’s online hackathon platform, Xathon, is an all-in-one solution for organizing a hackathon. The end-to-end platform lets businesses seamlessly organize hackathons for hiring or engaging employees.

Some of the features of Mercer | Mettl platform are:

- Personalization: Create a custom event page for the hackathon to increase awareness and engagement and streamline participation.

- Single dashboard: Easily schedule tasks or access information through a single dashboard.

- Collaborate with ease: Be it organizers, participants or judges, the Mercer | Mettl platform allows collaborating with other members easily.

Apart from these features, businesses also get access to a 24X7 support team that helps ensure seamless execution, making the hackathon a success.

## Conclusion

Whether businesses are looking for talented individuals to hire or want to generate ideas and engage employees, hackathons are the answer. Organizing an event may sound difficult with the planning involved, but the rewards are just as high. It helps engage the community, find talent, and boost morale.

## What is the David Ulrich Model?

The David Ulrich HR Model is meant specifically to organize human resources functions. This was developed by David Ulrich, who suggested that in giant organizations or large-scale businesses, HR functions should be compartmentalized into four segments.

More so, he stressed that shared service activities should be operated in call centers that have supporting technology or the internet that can provide the basic support and administrative functions to the rest of the business.

The goal of utilizing the Ulrich HR Competency Model is to make good and effective shifts from administrative management to strategic human resources. Although there are people who might question the efficiency and relevance of the Ulrich HR Model today, considering that it may be well past its prime, there are still a lot of businesses that find it a tangible part of business management.

### David Ulrich – “Father of Human Resources”

HR champion Dave Ulrich is no ordinary author as he is, in fact, looked upon as the great ‘father of human resources,’ according to HR Magazine. The dilemma today is that many people would claim that the Ulrich HR Competency Model could be impractical and insignificant in the 21st century or even beyond.

## Evolution of David Ulrich’s HR model

David Ulrich introduced his HR model in 1997, revolutionizing how organizations viewed the HR function. His original framework proposed that HR should operate through four key roles: strategic partner, change agent, administrative expert, and employee champion. This groundbreaking model offered a roadmap to transform HR into a strategic contributor rather than a purely administrative function.

Over the years, Ulrich has refined his thinking, responding to changing business contexts and the evolving nature of work. In the 2000s, the HR Business Partner (HRBP) concept took center stage, emphasizing a closer alignment of HR with business units. This era also saw the rise of Centers of Expertise and Shared Services, reinforcing specialization and efficiency in HR delivery.

In more recent years, Ulrich has shifted his focus toward HR competencies and HR’s impact on business value. He introduced the idea of outside-in HR, where HR must understand external business conditions, including customer expectations, economic trends, and stakeholder needs, and align internal HR practices accordingly. His updated frameworks increasingly emphasize agility, digital fluency, leadership development, and creating value for stakeholders beyond the enterprise, including communities and investors.

The evolution of Ulrich’s model reflects the growing complexity and influence of HR from an internal support function to a strategic, externally aware value creator in the modern organization.

## The four key roles in the David Ulrich HR model

The David Ulrich HR model allows businesses to streamline HR roles and responsibilities. Large organizations with huge teams can structure their working patterns and define clear roles for every team member and employee.

### Strategic partner

The strategic partner in the David Ulrich model focuses on blending HR processes and initiatives with the global business strategy. This ensures that HR strategies are cognizant of business results and contribute to a customer-centric approach. This role is the central channel for internal stakeholders to communicate with the HR department.

Additionally, strategic partners play a crucial role in identifying top talent within the organization and helping fill vacant positions. Furthermore, they share HR goals with the workforce and promote a harmonious and productive workplace environment.

### Change agent

The change agent supports the change and transition of a business, focusing on the human capital of the organization. When an organization is going through an expansion, evolution, or other changes, the change agent communicates these shifts internally. Therefore, this role requires deep knowledge of organizational culture to institutionalize the capacity for change effectively. It is accomplished through training individuals and empowering line managers to lead change initiatives.

The objective is to equip employees with the necessary skills to adapt to changing business goals and job roles. The change agent is crucial in preparing the entire organization for its next phase of growth.

### Administrative expert

The administrative expert creates efficient and effective HR processes that are customized according to the needs of businesses in a cost-effective manner. Over time, the role of administrative experts has evolved to focus on delivering high-quality services while also minimizing costs for the organization.

These experts stay updated on changes in legislation, regulations, occupational health and safety standards, and other labor and trade laws. This knowledge enables organizations to adopt policies and regulations to ensure compliance.

### Employee champion

Employee champions create a competent and committed workforce while keeping a strong emphasis on increasing human capital contribution. These professionals are knowledgeable about employee needs and how HR management can fulfill those needs.

Today, employee champions leverage digital design to enhance engagement and productivity, especially among the tech-savvy workforce. They advocate for employee interests and ensure that employees are supported during organizational changes.

Employee champions also utilize surveys to gauge employee satisfaction and identify any aspects of company culture that may affect employee productivity.

## How the David Ulrich HR model transforms the role of human resources

The Ulrich model of HRM has a wide impact on the role of HR in organizations. It redefines the priorities of HR and emphasizes the importance of HR professionals becoming true business partners. As a result of this transformation, several crucial changes occur within the HR profession:

### The focus on strategic implementation:

The model encourages HR professionals to adopt a strategic mindset, aiming to improve processes and activities that contribute to the success of the business rather than administrative tasks.

### Increase in collaboration:

HR professionals are now becoming business partners and working closely with other business functions to streamline their efforts with the organization’s overall strategy.

### Creation of new competencies:

The model encourages HR to build a diverse skill set, such as change management, strategic thinking, problem-solving, and financial acumen, to stand out in every type of role.

### Improvement in organizational value:

When HRs focus on activities and processes that add value to the organization, they can improve business performance, ensuring improved outcomes.

## Pros and cons of David Ulrich's HR model

### Pros:

- Strategic alignment: The Ulrich model shifts HR from being primarily administrative to becoming a strategic partner, aligning HR initiatives with business goals.

- Clear role definition: By dividing HR into four distinct roles – strategic partner, change agent, administrative expert, and employee champion – the model clarifies responsibilities and enhances accountability.

- Improved efficiency: The creation of shared service centers and centers of expertise allows for streamlined processes, reducing redundancy and driving operational efficiency.

- Enhanced employee experience: With a dedicated focus on being an employee champion, the model ensures employee advocacy and fosters a more engaging workplace.

- Business-focused HR: Encourages HR professionals to develop business acumen, ensuring that people practices contribute directly to organizational success.

### Cons:

- Implementation complexity: Successfully operationalizing the model requires significant structural change and stakeholder buy-in, which can be resource-intensive and disruptive.

- Role overlap and confusion: In practice, the four roles may blur, leading to role ambiguity, primarily in organizations lacking HR maturity.

- Underemphasis on culture: Critics argue that the model overlooks deeper cultural and relational aspects of HR, focusing too heavily on structure and roles.

- Scalability issues: Smaller organizations may find it challenging to adopt the model due to limited HR personnel or budgets.

- Over-structuring risks: There’s a risk of HR becoming overly bureaucratic and losing the human-centric touch that is vital in people management.

## The efficiency of the David Ulrich HR Competency Model

HR experts would contest that there is nothing wrong with the Ulrich Model, whether you decide to use it in any generation. However, the HR professionals who would use the Ulrich HR Competency Model without fully understanding how it functions may face challenges and bottlenecks.

As quoted in the HR Magazine, Ulrich explains, that people too often see the structure part of his theories as a ‘solution’ – something which, once implemented, will automatically deliver brilliant HR. “As with anything, the reality is of course much more nuanced. As with anything, it’s often not what you do, but how – or rather how intelligently – you do it,” he adds.

The Ulrich HR model is a blueprint meant to keep HR functions seamless; this does not translate into certain jobs. This is an all-too-common misconception of the Ulrich HR model, which creates a lot of confusion. This leaves many organizations dismantled in how they would balance transactions with customer expectations. Many HR practitioners fail to understand that transforming HR does not rely mainly on HR functions, but that senior management and the CEO also have important roles to play in making everything work.

Many companies still lack an integrated HR system to keep records organized, such as payroll, recruitment, talent or skills management, education, and training. These gaps create inefficiency in the administrative and management branches, which are key areas of the Ulrich model.

## Benefits of the David Ulrich model

The David Ulrich model offers various advantages, such as creating a responsive and adaptable HR organization, focusing on value-added activities, and enhancing HR professionals as strategic business partners. By balancing the four key roles of the model, HR leaders can ensure that their efforts are closely aligned with the organization’s overall strategy and objectives.

### Creating an adaptable organization:

The model encourages a shift from a siloed and task-oriented approach to a collaborative organizational structure. This shift allows HR professionals to be more attuned to the evolving needs of the business and adjust their strategies and tactics accordingly.

### Focusing on valuable activities:

By identifying and prioritizing high-impact activities, HR professionals can concentrate on initiatives that contribute to the organization’s success. This shift in focus on value-added activities empowers HR departments to demonstrate their strategic relevance and drive better business outcomes.

### Positioning HR professionals as strategic partners:

The Ulrich model positions HR professionals as valued business partners working closely with organizational leaders to achieve common objectives. This enables HR professionals to have a prominent influence in the organization, enabling them to ensure the right strategic direction.

### Aligning organizational strategy and objectives:

Through a balanced approach to the model, HR leaders need to sync their efforts with the organization’s strategic direction and objectives. This alignment helps HR make meaningful contributions to the attainment of business goals and demonstrate the strategic value of the function.

### Improving collaboration across the organization:

The model increases collaboration and communication between HR professionals and varied business functions. This collaborative approach enables HR to gain a deeper understanding of the organization’s needs, enable cross-functional collaboration, and drive initiatives to meet the organization’s strategic goals.

### Developing HR capabilities:

The Ulrich HR model of HRM makes the continuous development of diverse skills and capabilities necessary for HR professionals, enabling them to excel in each of the defined roles. This ongoing learning and growth allow HR professionals to stay abreast of industry best practices and bring innovative solutions to the organization.

### Improving employee satisfaction:

As employee champions, HR professionals are important for fostering employee engagement and satisfaction. Increased focus on understanding and addressing employee needs helps HR professionals cultivate a positive work environment that fosters engagement, retention, and high performance.

## Challenges faced by HRs and how to overcome them

### Resistance to change

The challenge: Shifting to the Ulrich model often means rethinking how HR works, and not everyone is quick to embrace change.

How to overcome it: Start with clear communication. Show how the model adds value. Try a phased rollout or pilot in one department to build momentum.

### Unclear roles

The challenge: With four distinct roles in the model, there’s a risk of overlap or confusion about who does what.

How to overcome it: Define each role clearly, including responsibilities, goals, and success metrics. Regular team check-ins and training can help keep everyone aligned.

### Skills gaps in the HR team

The challenge: Not every HR professional may be ready to take on strategic or change management roles immediately.

How to overcome it: Invest in learning and development. Offer training in business strategy, data analytics, and leadership. Encourage a growth mindset within the HR team.

### Lack of the right tools or systems

The challenge: The model works best when backed by strong HR technology and data systems, which many organizations may still lack.

How to overcome it: Start by modernizing core HR processes. Explore cloud-based tools or shared service platforms. Even minor upgrades can go a long way in driving efficiency.

### One-size-doesn’t-fit-all

The challenge: Smaller companies may struggle to implement the model in its complete form due to limited people and resources.

How to overcome it: Adapt the model to your scale. One person can handle multiple roles with clear priorities. Use outsourcing or automation to fill the gaps smartly.

### Too much focus on structure, not enough on culture

The challenge: It’s easy to get caught up in designing roles and processes and forget the human side of HR.

How to overcome it: Make culture part of the transformation. Listen to employees, build trust, and ensure leaders champion the change.

## Basic principles of the David Ulrich Competency Model

Despite the lingering confusion on its implementation, the principles surrounding the Ulrich model remain. These include:

- Creating a unified structure that delivers value

- Defining a clear distinction or role of HR

- Creating a competitive edge for the company

- Measuring how a company has performed as per the defined metrics

It is not a perfect system, but it provides a solid benchmark for an organization.

The most current study by Dave Ulrich, ‘Ulrich Comes of Age,’ marks the 18th founding anniversary of the ‘Human Resource Champions,’ which was published in 1996.

In the quest for HR efficiency, many organizations have invested in HR infrastructure, but they lack talent or skills management. There are no one-size-fits-all metrics that would mesh with any organization, as each company has its own unique needs. Organizations should look into the Dave Ulrich HR Competency Model as the standard but should try to innovate or be creative with a design that can be applicable to the organizational structure and changing needs.

## FAQs

### 2. What is the Ulrich model of the HR change agent?

### 3. What are Ulrich's five main areas of HR?

## Frequently asked questions (FAQs)

###

Online remote proctoring is a method of overseeing examinations conducted over the Internet. It employs technology to monitor test-takers in real time, ensuring exam security and integrity while allowing students to take assessments from remote locations.

###

Online proctored test work by monitoring test-takers' screens. The test takers must switch on their video and audio to verify their identity. They cannot start the exam before validating their ID. After the approval, the remote proctored exam begins, and an AI and/or a human proctor monitors the exam from start to finish. During the test, an ideal proctoring software monitors test-takers' screen activity, locks down web browsers, and enables the flagging of suspicious activities to prevent malpractices.

###

Yes, online proctoring often involves recording the screen to monitor exam activity and reduce instances of cheating. The proctoring software captures students’ screens alongside webcam and audio feeds during the exam.

###

Online test monitoring does not have the capability to detect other devices directly. However, it can monitor network activity, require the test-taker to use a specific browser, and utilize dual camera proctoring for a 360-degree view.

###

The three main types of proctored exams are:

  • Live online proctoring with a human invigilator monitoring candidates' screens in real-time.
  • Recorded online proctoring with AI monitoring, later reviewed by human proctors.
  • Advanced online proctoring without any human intervention, where advanced AI monitors and flags suspicious activities to score candidate integrity.

###

An online proctored exam utilizes technology and proctors to monitor the test-takers' screen activities. These examinations may have a human invigilator remotely supervising the test. A non-proctored exam is unsupervised and allows test takers to complete the test at their chosen time and pace. For this reason, remote proctoring ensures greater reliability and integrity in the test-taking and evaluation process compared to non-proctored exams.

###

Automated online exam proctoring uses artificial intelligence flags to prevent, detect, and gather evidence of any unwanted activity during an online exam.

###

Exam monitoring software is used to supervise people while they take an exam in online or remote settings. During the online test, a human proctor watches the session in real time and intervenes upon noticing suspicious behavior, such as someone else entering the room. Some exam monitoring combine human proctoring with automated monitoring such as AI. This type of proctoring is called hybrid proctoring. In hybrid proctoring, the automated system flags suspicious behavior and the human proctor who reviews those flags and intervenes when needed.

###

Mercer | Mettl SecureProctor seamlessly integrates with the user’s Learning Management System (LMS) to offer all our proctoring services. This integration ensures that users can easily implement effective monitoring and maintain exam integrity within their existing platform.

## Introduction

In the ever-evolving talent acquisition landscape, campus recruitment is a cornerstone for organizations seeking to secure top-tier talent from educational institutions. As businesses try to stay competitive in an increasingly dynamic market, campus recruitment strategies remain paramount. However, with the proliferation of options and the changing expectations of both employers and candidates, it becomes imperative for recruiters to refine their approach and adopt strategies that resonate with students.

This comprehensive guide delves into highly effective campus recruitment strategies to elevate the hiring game and attract bright minds to the organization. From leveraging technology to enhancing employer branding and fostering meaningful connections with students, these strategies are tailored to address the multifaceted challenges of campus recruitment in today’s fast-paced world.

## What is campus recruitment?

Campus recruitment involves hiring strategies to identify and hire top candidates for vacant positions in an organization. It includes step-by-step processes of campus identification, building a strong and impressionable recruitment team to visit colleges, organizing engagement activities, screening suitable candidates, and conducting interviews.

Identifying motivated individuals seeking learning and growth, bringing in new-age skills, and catalyzing a company’s development can be daunting. Organizations encounter several challenges in building a successful and scalable campus hiring strategy. These challenges range from making several campus visits and aligning stakeholders’ schedules to managing time and investing resources to conduct the drive. As a result, HR leaders need a high-yielding campus hiring strategy that works as efficiently as an on-site campus drive and spouts notable results.

## Why do organizations need it?

Campus recruitment enables organizations to engage in strategic workforce planning. It helps find better-qualified candidates and build a stronger connection with post-graduate and graduate students.

By engaging in campus recruitment initiatives, companies gain direct access to this pool of fresh and soon-to-be graduates, allowing them to identify and attract candidates with suitable skills and knowledge needed to thrive in respective fields and industries.

## Campus hiring strategy: Challenges

The campus recruitment process presents numerous challenges for hiring professionals. Some of them are:

- Time consumption: Campus recruitment demands significant time investment, encompassing scheduling visits to various educational institutions, coordinating with faculty and students, and executing rigorous screening processes. This process extends further with the need to review resumes meticulously, conduct interviews, and manage candidate communication. Additionally, travel between campuses increases the time expenditure, especially for companies targeting candidates from diverse geographic regions.

- Manual effort: Manual labor remains a crucial challenge in campus recruitment, particularly in tasks like processing resumes, inputting candidate data into systems, and organizing paperwork. Coordinating interviews, scheduling meetings, and maintaining communication with candidates involve substantial manual effort, often through emails, phone calls, and face-to-face interactions. Not using automated systems further exacerbates this challenge, necessitating meticulous attention to detail to ensure accuracy and compliance throughout the recruitment process.

## How to build an effective campus hiring strategy?

Campus hiring strategies are crucial in recruiting top talents. Here are fifteen effective campus hiring strategies to boost hiring:

### A. Research

Comprehensive research is the key to an effective campus hiring strategy. Understanding the hiring competencies and roles helps determine the campuses to target, the hiring partner required, and the overall process. A list of methods that one must adopt while conducting pre-campus recruitment research follows:

1. Building a hiring plan

The preliminary step to building an effective campus hiring strategy is listing hiring needs. Understanding organizational needs helps roll out relevant job positions effectively. Measuring the company’s workforce requirements by receiving input from team leaders of various departments is the first step. It is critical to understand the workload distribution and the short-term team member requirements for upcoming projects, followed by a comprehensive understanding of the current attrition rates in the key departments. HR professionals can understand the skills gap among the current workforce by implementing skills gap analysis solutions to gain data-driven results. A step-by-step approach assimilating the abovementioned factors helps determine the existing workforce challenges and create a viable hiring plan.

2. Selecting a hiring partner

As the next step, identifying the recruitment partner can reduce the workload substantially. A hiring partner provides easy access to resources, marketing ideas, and technical skills, frontloading the entire gamut of the hiring process. Using various hiring methods, a hiring partner helps find top talents to finalize candidates for job positions.

3. Building campus intelligence

Building campus intelligence requires organizations to collate the data and experiences of conducting campus hiring in past years and analyze the outcomes. This helps attribute scores to each campus regarding how the students perform in their assessments or how many students fall within the preferred salary range of an organization. Campus intelligence also involves creating a competency heat map, whereby each campus’s overall students’ performance can be mapped onto the competencies prevalent in the industry and then assigned to the competency requirements of individual organizations.

4. Building a strong recruitment team

A campus hiring drive is one of the astute means of creating a solid brand presence. Therefore, building an impressive recruitment team is one of the best practices for recruiting college students. A team of engaged employees aligned to the company’s goals can represent the organization suitably. Employee engagement strategies offer insights into which team members should participate in the recruitment program.

### B. Promotion

A well-thought-out promotion strategy ensures successful campus hiring. From reaching out to students through social media to creating an attractive careers page and promoting recruitment drives through rewarding programs, one must clearly define job descriptions to attract the most suitable participants.

5. Advertising right

Recruiters can leverage social media platforms like Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook, Quora, etc., to market campus recruitment drives among college students. One can innovate new ways to announce the recruitment drive through a catchy banner or an engaging short video. A robust social media presence is a remarkable way to attract the talent pool. Organizations can keep the messaging short and crisp with captivating content that can be sustained on the careers webpage and linked to the social media pages.

6. Innovating with a career page

Hiring professionals can attract candidates with a creative and interactive careers page on the organization's website with compelling headlines highlighting the organization’s qualities, company’s work culture, goals, benefits, rewards, etc. The visual content could include images, employee videos or graphics to create a story. A well-designed job description can influence students’ decisions. Adding value to the job description by explaining profiles well attracts more candidates for the job role.

7. Building a campus ambassador program

Another innovative campus recruitment strategy adopted by companies is the Campus Ambassador Program. It is a creative way for brands to enhance awareness about their services through university students. In these programs, the brand identifies enthusiastic students willing to learn. Then, mentors and teachers are assigned to teach them different skills, enabling students to understand the company's technologies and how things are executed. These campus ambassadors then help other students to make career decisions by conducting workshops and seminars for the brand.

8. Adopting a student referral program

“Word of mouth” is one of the most valuable marketing efforts. Using a referral program, one can identify talent using the current students' social networks. Employers can build a program in which they pay a referral fee to their current employees, encouraging them to recommend potential candidates for vacant positions. Student referral programs work similarly, improving the quality of hire and time-to-hire and reducing cost-per-hire. It helps boost the company’s brand and enhance the employer's reputation.

### C. Engagement

Connecting and engaging with students assists in impactful campus hiring. Nurturing a connection with students is critical for any brand to create a strong presence. One can pre-engage, connect with students, and spread awareness about the brand by hosting interactive ‘ask me anything’ sessions. Interactive hackathons can also capture their attention and identify their abilities before commencing the recruitment process.

9. Pre-placement connect

Businesses employ pre-placement interactions and presentations even before commencing the placement drive. Companies can build the brand's image and highlight its propositions by visiting the campus. One must develop the company's brand visibility through engaging presentations. Alums can undertake such interactions to create a more substantial impact. From hosting information sessions to allowing students to ask questions about the company, establishing a robust brand image helps candidates recognize the company and excites them about prospects.

10. Pre-placement engagement

One of the most engaging ways to source candidates and build a unique brand identity is through innovative contests, such as hackathons, ideathons or case study competitions. These tools are excellent platforms to exhibit the company’s unique culture, technology, learning opportunities, and challenges. Such contests allow students to experience the brand closely. Hackathons, ideathons and case study competitions create a business simulation to help assess the students’ actual on-ground skills. The rewards can be an additional attraction. One can execute these contests online seamlessly without employing a dedicated team to set up a base on the campus. A student ambassador can drive engagement and participation, ensuring a smooth experience.

### D. Skills assessment

The most crucial step in a campus recruitment drive is skills assessment. With efficient tools to assess candidates, one can tap into the student’s potential by conducting high-yielding assessments for diverse roles. It helps evaluate and filter students based on their skills and find a suitable way to proceed with the drive ahead.

11. Assessment tools

Effective screening assessments can significantly impact an organization’s hiring quality. Screening assessment results have a direct correlation with on-job performance and culture fitment. Data can be analyzed using new-age screening assessments and tools to predict hiring outcomes. These holistically virtual tools, powered by AI and remote proctoring, evaluate students on multiple levels of aptitude, communication skills, domain skills, personality traits, etc. A customizable set of assessments that measures all aspects of a potential employee, such as agility and domain-specific knowledge, can improve the hiring quality and onboarding rate. Assessments are also practical filter tools that enable organizations to select top candidates.

Companies must streamline the campus hiring process and lend it a structured approach by employing the following screening assessments:

- Technical Assessments: These assessments enable filtering the top talent with in-depth functional knowledge. The test makes applicants look at multiple problems comprehensively to offer a solution. Employers could also use a coding simulator, an innovative tool to simulate an actual coding problem, to assess a candidate's problem-solving skills in a real-life work scenario.

- Communication Skills Assessments: This assessment measures an applicant’s expertise in English language-based communication. Such a test comprises sections that evaluate an individual’s speaking, writing, reading, and listening skills, including comprehension, pronunciation, vocabulary and fluency.

- Aptitude Assessments: This assessment can be employed in the hiring process to find candidates with excellent problem-solving skills and numerical abilities quickly and efficiently. These online assessments evaluate critical thinking and reasoning skills using questions.

12. Simulator-based screening

Simulator-based tests are unique interactive tests assessing candidates’ problem-solving and coding skills. They are one of the most used coding skill tests as employers get a detailed insight into the candidates’ problem-solving abilities in real-life situations. A candidate is provided with a comprehensive abstract problem to find solutions. Backed by an auto-grading system, the results are data-driven and credible. Simulation tests serve as an effective strategy for campus recruitment by identifying and hiring the best coders.

### E. Structured interviews

Interviews are the ultimate step in a campus recruitment drive. After shortlisting candidates with assessments, one can apply the following filters for a refined outcome with structured interviews.

13. Conducting compelling virtual interviews

One must conduct structured interviews as a part of the campus hiring process, where the hiring manager creates questions focusing on the organization’s present and future competency needs. In the case of technical hiring, evaluating the candidates’ technical skills is critical. For example, pair programming interviews can help employers expedite technical skills assessment by assessing candidates based on real-time programming skills. Pair programming interviews are backed by an online interview platform, pre-embedded with a coding simulator. The platform allows candidates to solve a real-world problem during the interview, where the interviewer can invigilate and evaluate their proficiencies in real time. These virtual interviews are location-agnostic and can be used to hire candidates for technical departments.

### F. Post-hire measures

Successful onboarding is fundamental to engaging and retaining new team members after a successful campus hiring process. Building an interactive plan to make the new joiner feel comfortable in the team and the company is essential. The next step is to measure the effectiveness of the campus hiring drive to adapt and innovate for future campaigns.

14. Virtual onboarding

Virtual onboarding should be engaging, straightforward and stress-free. It is essential to accommodate the requirements of remote employees, such as laptops, monitors and headsets; upload the new hires’ paperwork into signing software and use the new hires’ email addresses to send them everything they need to sign before their joining date. Using videoconferencing software for virtual face-to-face meetings with team members helps put a face to a name. It makes the new team members feel like a part of the team. Virtual onboarding games are another fun way to introduce the company to a new workforce. The games can be built around the company’s values and vision. A virtual scavenger hunt or games like ‘two truths, one lie’ could help develop and sustain new employees’ interests.

15. Measure the effectiveness

It is critical to measure the effectiveness of the campus recruiting strategy. It can be done by analyzing how the candidates are hired, assessing whether it was through a student referral program or a hackathon event, the number of offers accepted, the retention rate of new hires, and the cost-effectiveness of the drive. In addition, determining the number of people hired vis-à-vis the set target and how efficiently the newly hired workforce performs helps develop a roadmap for future strategies.

## Stages of campus recruitment strategy

The campus recruitment strategy can be divided into five stages. They are:

- Identifying needs and selecting campuses: Organizations must understand why they should hire on campus and identify the problem that needs solutions. After that, campus recruiters must shortlist the colleges they wish to visit.

- Building suitable assessment solutions: The assessment of candidates is significant in any hiring strategy, including campus hiring. Some common assessment tools can include aptitude tests, technical tests, coding skills tests, etc. These tests assist in filtering and finding the candidate suited for the position.

- Connecting and advertising with career centers: University career services or placement committees are the bridge between organizations and candidates. They can provide relevant information about past programs, helping recruiters analyze data and build better strategies.

- Evaluating and interviewing applicants: After shortlisting candidates, recruiters must assess and schedule interviews for the final shortlisted candidates. The strategy should state the assessment type, the number of selection rounds, and the judgment criteria, and it should be communicated to the career centers so that candidates applying for the role know what to expect when they sign up for the event. Post interviews, recruiters can conduct one-on-one interactions to make a final decision.

- Extending offers to selected applicants: After the final interview, recruiters can send the offer letters to the campus hires. It should include all essential details, like joining date, designation, location, etc. Organizations can also opt for campus recruiting software to streamline the process, like an online tool that can roll out multiple offers to many candidates in one go.

## Campus hiring strategy: Benefits

Campus hiring provides many benefits to companies and candidates. Some of them are:

- Broader talent pool: The college recruiting process provides a vast talent pool, enabling organizations to hire top candidates and bring new ideas and diversity to the organization.

- Stronger relationships: Through campus recruitment programs, organizations can build long-lasting relationships with colleges.

- Cost-effectiveness: When organizations use digital tools, campus hiring strategies help save resources. Hiring drives allow organizations to connect with many candidates in one single event.

- Higher onboarding rate: Campus recruitment usually has a better onboarding and retention rate than traditional hiring methods. In campus hires, candidates are more motivated.

- Eagerness to learn: Entry-level employees are loyal to their organizations and keen to learn and experiment. They offer a fresh outlook and are more comfortable working with new technologies.

## Conclusion

Campuses are a gold mine of fresh talent possessing new-age skills, curiosity and an elevated level of motivation. Organizations can easily tap into this talent pool by inculcating the right set of campus hiring strategies. Right from building a connection with students to assessing their skills as per the job role and then finally onboarding, attracting the finest talent demands structured planning. Organizations that do not value measuring their campus hiring strategies that determine the quality of their hires lack the most significant basics. Such anomalies can have long-term consequences, especially in a fast market where companies continuously vie to attract the best and brightest.

Campus recruitment strategies help recruitment professionals prepare for talent that offers many possibilities. The placement season pressurizes students and talent acquisition professionals equally. ## Frequently asked questions (FAQs)
